2027-campaign-tinubu-reform-test-aljazee.title: 2027 Campaign Season Opens With Tinubu Facing Reform Test
2027-campaign-tinubu-reform-test-aljazee.excerpt: As Nigeria’s pre-2027 election campaign period begins, President Bola Tinubu faces growing scrutiny over the economy and insecurity, including a surge in mass kidnappings.
paras: Nigeria’s campaign season ahead of the 2027 general election is opening with President Bola Tinubu facing a significant test over his economic reforms and the country’s security situation, according to an Al Jazeera report.

The report highlights the strain rising prices have placed on ordinary Nigerians — with traders and consumers cutting back on routine purchases — and notes growing criticism over insecurity, including a surge in mass kidnappings across the country.

abiodun-pdp-adc-defectors-apc-ogun-east..title: Abiodun Receives Hundreds of PDP, ADC Defectors Into APC, Mobilises Ogun East for 2027
abiodun-pdp-adc-defectors-apc-ogun-east..excerpt: Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun has received hundreds of PDP and ADC members into the APC at a reception in Ijebu-Ode, consolidating the party’s hold on Ogun East ahead of the 2027 elections.
paras: Ogun State Governor and leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prince Dapo Abiodun, has formally welcomed hundreds of former members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and African Democratic Congress (ADC) — including party leaders from the nine local government areas of Ogun East Senatorial District — into the ruling party.

The defectors were received at an elaborate reception held at the Ojude-Oba carnival ground in Ijebu-Ode, filled to capacity with APC members, supporters and new entrants. Welcoming them, Abiodun said their decision showed they had “seen the light,” and assured them of equal treatment and full integration into the party.

The governor pointed to his administration’s record since 2019, saying more than 100 roads had been built across Ogun East, and listed projects including the Gateway International Airport and the Olokola Deep Sea Port. Ogun APC Chairman Chief Yemi Sanusi attributed the influx of opposition members to the administration’s performance, while the defectors pledged loyalty and vowed to work for the party’s victory in 2027.

adedimeji-mo-bimpe-triplets-thanksgiving.title: Lateef Adedimeji & Mo Bimpe Hold Thanksgiving for Triplets
adedimeji-mo-bimpe-triplets-thanksgiving.excerpt: Nollywood actors Lateef Adedimeji and Mo Bimpe held a thanksgiving service to celebrate the birth of their triplets, after years of public scrutiny over their journey to parenthood.
paras: Nollywood actors Lateef Adedimeji and his wife, actress Mo Bimpe, held a grand thanksgiving service to celebrate the birth of their triplets, with provisions made for fans to join the celebration virtually.

Adedimeji expressed gratitude for the arrival of the couple's three sons, reflecting on years of public scrutiny and, at times, mockery the couple faced over their journey to parenthood before welcoming their children.
The celebration has drawn warm messages from across the Nigerian entertainment industry, with fans and colleagues celebrating the couple's long-awaited joy.

adeleke-campaign-inec-ebonyi-rec-osun.ht.title: Adeleke Campaign Council Demands INEC Explanation Over Ebonyi REC's Presence in Osun
adeleke-campaign-inec-ebonyi-rec-osun.ht.excerpt: Governor Adeleke's Imole Campaign Council has questioned the presence of Ebonyi State's REC in Osun ahead of Saturday's election, saying she wasn't on the official list of deployed officials.
paras: The Imole Campaign Council of Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has raised concerns over the alleged presence of the Resident Electoral Commissioner for Ebonyi State, Pauline Ugoyenka, in Osun ahead of Saturday's governorship election.

The campaign council urged the Independent National Electoral Commission to clarify Ugoyenka's presence in the state, arguing her name did not appear on the list of RECs officially deployed to Osun for the August 15 poll. According to the council, an INEC letter dated August 3 identified officials and states providing supervisory contingents for the election from 15 contributing states, and Ebonyi was not among them.

The council, through the Chairman of its Media and Publicity Committee, Bamidele Salam, demanded immediate clarification from INEC on the production and verification of ballot papers and result sheets to be used in the election. "We therefore demand immediate clarification from INEC and insist that only properly customised ballot papers and result sheets specifically produced and verified for the Osun governorship election must be used," the statement said, adding that the council would not accept any arrangement capable of compromising the transparency of the vote.

adeleke-receives-certificate-of-return-o.title: Adeleke Receives Certificate of Return, Pledges Scholarships for Electoral Violence Victims
adeleke-receives-certificate-of-return-o.excerpt: Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke received his Certificate of Return from INEC and pledged scholarships for the children of those affected by electoral violence.
paras: Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke on Wednesday received his Certificate of Return from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), following his victory in the August 15 governorship election.
At the event, the governor promised scholarships for the children of victims of electoral violence during the poll.
The certificate formalises his re-election, even as the opposition All Progressives Congress has said it does not accept the result and is reviewing the electoral records.

african-airlines-reject-api-pnr-charges..title: African Airlines Reject Charges for Border Security Data Systems
african-airlines-reject-api-pnr-charges..excerpt: Aviation bodies including IATA and AFRAA have rejected attempts to make airlines and passengers pay for government-run passenger data systems, saying border security is a state responsibility.
paras: African airlines and their industry representatives have pushed back against attempts to make carriers and passengers pay for government-run Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) systems, insisting that border security funding is the responsibility of states.

In a joint statement, the African Airlines Association, Airlines Association of Southern Africa, and International Air Transport Association said they support the deployment of API and PNR systems across the continent but warned the cost should not be passed to travellers or carriers. The associations cited ICAO's Policies on Charges for Airports and Air Navigation Services, which they said establishes border security as a government responsibility.

"Imposing API and PNR fees on airlines to fund government border security programs increases the cost of travel, undermines connectivity, and weakens the economic benefits that aviation generates through tourism, trade, and investment," the associations said, urging African governments to establish clear legal and operational frameworks, including data protection safeguards, before implementing the systems.

amnesty-fadahunsi-name-shame-150-countri.title: Amnesty International Vows to "Name and Shame" Senator Fadahunsi in 150 Countries
amnesty-fadahunsi-name-shame-150-countri.excerpt: Amnesty International Nigeria says it will publicize Senator Francis Fadahunsi's case across 150 countries, calling him an example in its campaign against politicians who incite electoral violence.
paras: Amnesty International Nigeria says it will publicize the case of Senator Francis Fadahunsi across the 150 countries where it operates, calling him an example in its campaign against politicians who incite electoral violence.

Country Director Isa Sanusi made the comments on Channels Television's Sunrise Daily, reacting to a viral video in which Fadahunsi, who represents Osun East, appeared to direct supporters to "kill" members of the rival Accord Party ahead of Saturday's Osun governorship election. "We had so many terrible politicians say terrible things ahead of elections, but this one is exceptional... advocacy of hatred is a crime under international law as well as Nigerian laws," Sanusi said.

Fadahunsi has denied calling for violence; while he initially said the video was edited to distort his meaning, he has more recently claimed it was generated using artificial intelligence. Amnesty said it would also target politicians who hire religious figures to incite violence on either side of Nigeria's religious divide. The warning comes amid separate reports from human rights lawyer Femi Falana alleging at least 30 people have been killed in politically motivated violence in Osun State in the weeks leading up to the election.

angelique-kidjo-hollywood-walk-of-fame-s.title: Angélique Kidjo Becomes First African Artist Honoured With Hollywood Walk of Fame Star
angelique-kidjo-hollywood-walk-of-fame-s.excerpt: Benin-born global music star Angélique Kidjo has been celebrated as making history with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
paras: Benin-born global music icon Angélique Kidjo has been celebrated for making history with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, a milestone widely hailed across African media as a landmark moment for African music.

The multiple Grammy-winning artist, known for a decades-long career blending West African traditions with global genres, was congratulated by fans and outlets who described the honour as a historic recognition.

apc-osun-mega-rally.html.title: APC Chieftains Arrive Osun for Election Mega Rally
apc-osun-mega-rally.html.excerpt: Senate President Akpabio, Governors Uzodimma and Aiyedatiwa, and other APC chieftains have arrived in Osun ahead of a mega campaign rally before Saturday's election.
paras: Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, and other senior APC figures have arrived in Osun State ahead of a mega rally for the party's governorship candidate, days before Saturday's election.

The rally forms part of a final push by the APC to mobilise support in what has become one of the most closely watched and tense state elections of the year, with both major parties intensifying campaign activity in the closing days before the vote.
The visit comes amid heightened security concerns in the state, with police and other agencies stepping up election-security operations ahead of Saturday's polls.

apc-rejects-adeleke-victory-osun-audit.h.title: Osun Election: APC Rejects Adeleke’s Victory, Begins Audit of Results
apc-rejects-adeleke-victory-osun-audit.h.excerpt: The All Progressives Congress says it does not accept INEC’s declaration of Governor Ademola Adeleke as winner, and has launched a review of the electoral records.
paras: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has rejected the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) declaration of Ademola Adeleke as winner of the Osun State governorship election, insisting the governor did not secure the highest number of valid votes.

Speaking on Arise News, the party’s Director-General of the Osun Governorship Campaign, Oluwole Oke, said the APC had begun an audit of the electoral process before deciding its next move. “We do not agree with the declaration of INEC. That’s our position for now. We believe he did not score the highest valid votes,” Oke said.
He said the party had directed its agents to submit copies of Forms EC8A, EC8B and EC8C for review, and that it would examine the election against the Electoral Act before taking a formal position.

INEC had declared Adeleke winner with 511,067 votes to APC candidate Bola Oyebamiji’s 444,815 — a margin of 66,252 votes — with the governor carrying 19 of Osun’s 30 local government areas. President Bola Tinubu has already congratulated Adeleke.

apm-pdp-candidates-withdraw-endorse-adel.title: APM, PDP Candidates Withdraw From Osun Race, Endorse Adeleke
apm-pdp-candidates-withdraw-endorse-adel.excerpt: Two governorship candidates have withdrawn from Saturday's Osun election and endorsed incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, a day before Nigerians head to the polls.
paras: Two governorship candidates in Saturday's Osun State election have withdrawn from the race and thrown their support behind incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, a day before Nigerians head to the polls.

Adebayo Simon Adewale of the Allied Peoples Movement announced his withdrawal at a press conference in Osogbo on Thursday, saying the decision followed "deep reflection and extensive consultation" with party leaders and stakeholders. "I hereby declare my full support for the re-election of His Excellency, Senator Ademola Jackson Nurudeen Adeleke," he said, framing the move as being about "the future of Osun" rather than personal ambition.

In a separate announcement, PDP candidate Adedamola Adebayo, popularly known as "Fryo," also withdrew and endorsed Adeleke, urging PDP members and supporters to back the incumbent governor. The withdrawal clarifies an earlier point of confusion: a PDP faction had issued a statement claiming a court victory for Adebayo's candidacy just a day before he confirmed, in his own words, that he was standing down. Adeleke now faces APC's Bola Oyebamiji and ADC's Najeem Salaam as his main rivals heading into Saturday's vote.

araujo-liverpool-loan-barcelona.html.title: Ronald Araujo Set for Liverpool Loan From Barcelona
araujo-liverpool-loan-barcelona.html.excerpt: Liverpool are finalising a loan move for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo, with the club set to cover his full salary.
paras: Liverpool are moving to complete a loan deal for Barcelona centre-back Ronald Araujo, with the transfer said to be firmly in motion after weeks of talks.

Under the terms being finalised, Araujo will join on loan while Liverpool cover his full salary, understood to be around €11 million net. Barcelona director Deco reportedly made the loan structure a condition of the move, giving Araujo assurances over regular game time, something the Uruguayan has been keen to secure after a stop-start role in Catalonia.
The move would add significant defensive experience to Liverpool's squad as they look to strengthen their backline ahead of the new season.

aregbesola-loses-polling-unit-apc.html.title: Aregbesola Humiliated as APC Wins His Own Polling Unit Despite Backing ADC
aregbesola-loses-polling-unit-apc.html.excerpt: APC's Bola Oyebamiji defeated ADC at former Osun Governor Rauf Aregbesola's own polling unit, a symbolic setback since Aregbesola serves as the ADC's national secretary.
paras: The All Progressives Congress defeated the African Democratic Congress at the polling unit of former Osun State Governor Rauf Aregbesola in Saturday's governorship election, delivering a symbolic setback in the stronghold of one of the ADC's leading national figures.

At Polling Unit 001, Cooperative Building Junction, Isare, Ward 08, Ilesa East Local Government Area, APC candidate Bola Oyebamiji secured 256 votes to emerge first. Incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party came second with 43 votes, while ADC candidate Najeem Salaam, who Aregbesola has publicly backed, polled just 13 votes. The APC also won a second polling unit near Aregbesola's family compound, 202 votes to Accord's 110 and ADC's 12.

Aregbesola, who governed Osun from 2010 to 2018 and later served as Minister of Interior under the APC before defecting to the ADC, is the party's national secretary and one of its most prominent figures in the state. The APC went on to win Ilesa East local government overall, with Oyebamiji polling 16,208 votes to Adeleke's 12,280, while Aregbesola's ADC managed just 504 votes in the LGA.

army-15-brigade-dismantle-ipob-esn-anamb.title: Army's New 15 Brigade Dismantles 3 IPOB/ESN Camps in Anambra, Rescues 6 Children
army-15-brigade-dismantle-ipob-esn-anamb.excerpt: Troops of the newly established 15 Brigade dismantled three IPOB/ESN camps in Anambra State, killing three suspects and recovering six children found with detained accomplices.
paras: Troops of the newly established 15 Brigade, Nigerian Army, operating under Joint Task Force South East's Operation UDO KA, dismantled three suspected IPOB/ESN camps and recovered weapons, explosives, and other logistics during a coordinated operation in Anambra State.

The intelligence-led operation was conducted in the early hours of Saturday following credible information on IPOB/ESN elements operating from camps at Osuakwa, along the boundary between Ihiala and Ogbaru Local Government Areas. Troops of 15 Brigade, working alongside the DSS and the Agunechemba Vigilante Group, launched a coordinated dawn raid and came under hostile fire before overwhelming the attackers in a fierce firefight.

Three suspected IPOB/ESN members were killed, and the three camps were overrun and destroyed. Recovered items included an FN rifle with ammunition, a pump-action shotgun, 15 sticks of dynamite, four motorcycles, and communication equipment. Further exploitation led to the arrest of a suspect identified as Chijioke along with two accomplices, who were found in the company of six children.

article-1.html.title: Army Rescues Nine Kidnapped Commuters Along Kogi’s Ajaokuta–Itobe Road
article-1.html.excerpt: Troops of the Nigerian Army rescued nine commuters, including an infant, after a gun battle with kidnappers near Adumu community in Kogi State.
paras: The Nigerian Army has rescued nine commuters abducted by suspected kidnappers along the Ajaokuta–Itobe Road in Ofu Local Government Area of Kogi State, in the second major rescue operation reported in the area within two days.

In a statement posted to its official X account, the Army said troops of 21 Battalion, deployed at Patrol Base Itobe, responded to a distress report of an attack on commuters along the route. On arrival, they found a Toyota Hiace bus and a Toyota Sienna abandoned by the roadside, with the passengers already taken away.

The troops launched a pursuit operation, tracing the kidnappers' withdrawal route to the outskirts of Adumu community in neighbouring Dekina Local Government Area, where they engaged the suspects in a gun battle. The Army said the exchange forced the kidnappers to abandon their captives and flee into the surrounding bush.

The nine rescued victims — two elderly men, two elderly women, four men, and an infant — were evacuated to safety and handed over to the Nigeria Police's Itobe Area Command for further action and reunification with their families.

The rescue follows a separate operation two days earlier, on August 9, in which a joint team of soldiers, naval personnel, police, local vigilantes, and hunters rescued 16 people abducted along the nearby Ojuwo–Ajengo–Memarebo and Ojiwo–Itobe roads. One hunter was killed during that earlier operation. Together, the two rescues account for 25 people freed from the same general area within a single week, underscoring how frequently the Ofu–Dekina axis has become a target for roadside kidnapping gangs.

The Army said troops remained in pursuit of the fleeing kidnappers, with coordinated search operations ongoing to recover any remaining victims and apprehend those responsible. It reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and property in collaboration with other security agencies, and urged the public to share timely, credible information that could help rapid-response efforts.

article-2.html.title: Super Falcons Knocked Out of WAFCON 2026, Miss Automatic World Cup Ticket
article-2.html.excerpt: Nigeria's ten-time African champions lost 1-0 to Cameroon in the WAFCON quarter-final, missing out on automatic qualification for the 2027 World Cup.
paras: Nigeria's Super Falcons have been eliminated from the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations after a 1-0 defeat to Cameroon in the quarter-final at the Larbi Zaouli Stadium in Casablanca, ending the defending champions' title defence earlier than expected.

The result also cost Nigeria automatic qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil — a prize that had been on the line for both sides going into the tie. Nigeria will instead have to negotiate the African playoff route to keep their World Cup hopes alive, extending an unbroken run of appearances at every edition of the tournament since it began in 1991.

It marks the first time the ten-time African champions have failed to reach at least the semi-finals of a centralised WAFCON tournament, and comes after a shaky group stage in which Nigeria lost their opening match to debutants Malawi before recovering with wins over Zambia and a 6-2 thrashing of Egypt to scrape through in second place.

Cameroon, by contrast, arrived unbeaten, having topped their group with wins over Mali and Ghana before a draw with Cape Verde. The Indomitable Lionesses had lost nine of their previous eleven meetings with Nigeria, including a 1-0 defeat to the Super Falcons in the quarter-finals of the 2022 edition — but this time held firm behind a goalkeeper who produced a string of crucial saves to deny Nigeria an equaliser, including a header from Uchenna Kanu in the second half.

Cameroon's win sets up a semi-final against tournament hosts Morocco, and confirms their own place at the 2027 World Cup. For Nigeria, attention now turns to a play-off against South Africa for one of the continent's remaining World Cup qualification spots.

article-3.html.title: Daddy Showkey Credits Akpabio With Helping Him Walk Again After Spinal Injury
article-3.html.excerpt: Veteran singer Daddy Showkey has revealed how Senate President Godswill Akpabio helped him recover after a car crash left him unable to walk for three years.
paras: Veteran Nigerian musician John Asiemo, popularly known as Daddy Showkey, has revealed how Senate President Godswill Akpabio stood by him during one of the most difficult periods of his life — a car crash that left him unable to walk for three years.

Speaking on The Podcast Network, the Ajegunle-born "galala" pioneer said the accident severely damaged his spine and confined him to bed for an extended stretch of his recovery. "My spine failed. I could not walk for three years. I had a car accident," he said. "It was before the assassination attempts."

Showkey said Akpabio, who was not yet Senate President at the time, was among the first people to respond when the accident happened. "The person who first came to my rescue was Godswill Akpabio," he said. "He helped me to go to the hospital, and I was in hospital for three years. He played a lot of roles. I knew him before he became a commissioner, and he is a true friend. When that thing happened to me, if not for Godswill Akpabio, I would not have walked again."

The revelation adds a personal dimension to a friendship that predates both men's rise to their current public profiles, and comes as Showkey has been increasingly open in recent interviews about the string of near-death experiences that have shaped his life — including separate assassination attempts he says he survived in the years following his recovery.

Showkey, whose 1990s hits helped define the ghetto/galala sound that grew out of Ajegunle, remains an active voice in Nigerian music and continues to speak publicly about his path from a difficult upbringing to national recognition.

asuu-20-universities-strike-ultimatum.ht.title: ASUU Authorises 20 Universities to Prepare for Strike Over Unimplemented Agreement
asuu-20-universities-strike-ultimatum.ht.excerpt: ASUU has authorised branches in 20 universities to issue 14-day strike ultimatums, citing government failure to implement the 2025 FGN-ASUU Agreement. Two universities have already gone on strike.
paras: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) has authorised branches in 20 Nigerian universities to issue 14-day strike ultimatums to their respective authorities, citing the federal and state governments' failure to fully implement the 2025 FGN-ASUU Agreement.

The decision was reached at ASUU's National Executive Council (NEC) meeting held at the University of Abuja on August 8 and 9. ASUU President, Professor Christopher Piwuna, said the union was concerned about what it called the "haphazard implementation" of the agreement, particularly the federal government's delay in releasing the subvention needed to fully actualise it.

Affected institutions include Nasarawa State University, Kaduna State University, Imo State University, Gombe State University, Plateau State University, Ambrose Alli University, and several others across the country. According to reports, only about 10 state universities have fully implemented the renegotiated agreement, leaving more than 57 others yet to comply.

Two universities have already gone further than the ultimatum stage: branches at Imo State University and Nasarawa State University commenced indefinite strikes this week, disrupting academic activity on both campuses. The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has urged ASUU to direct its pressure at the governments responsible rather than shutting down institutions, warning that repeated strikes cause "prolonged academic disruptions" for students. Piwuna said an emergency NEC meeting will be held in late August or early September to review the situation.

atiku-questions-fg-borrowing-oil-windfal.title: Atiku Questions FG Borrowing Amid Alleged N7.98tn Oil Windfall
atiku-questions-fg-borrowing-oil-windfal.excerpt: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has criticised continued government borrowing despite what he calls a N7.98 trillion oil revenue windfall. The Presidency has rejected the claim.
paras: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has criticised the Federal Government's continued domestic borrowing, questioning why the administration is raising debt despite what he describes as an estimated N7.98 trillion windfall from oil prices trading well above the 2026 budget benchmark.

In a statement issued by his aide, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the government had already raised about N5 trillion from the domestic bond market in the first half of 2026, nearly 80 percent of the total borrowed over the same period last year. "Nigerians deserve a full accounting of this windfall. Where has the money gone?" he asked, calling for transparent disclosure of proceeds from excess crude sales.

The Presidency has rejected the claim. Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, dismissed Atiku's analysis as "deficient," insisting no such oil windfall exists and challenging the former vice-president to provide evidence for his figures.

aviation-strike-lagos-abuja-airports.htm.title: Aviation Workers' Strike Grounds Flights, Strands Passengers in Lagos and Abuja
aviation-strike-lagos-abuja-airports.htm.excerpt: Aviation unions shut down operations at several domestic airlines on Tuesday over unremitted ticket charges and unionisation disputes, stranding thousands of travellers.
paras: Thousands of travellers were stranded at Nigeria's major airports on Tuesday after aviation unions shut down operations at several domestic airlines over unresolved labour disputes.

The strike, led by the National Union of Air Transport Employees (NUATE), the Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (ATSSSAN), and the National Association of Aircraft Pilots and Engineers (NAAPE), backed by the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC), saw union members barricade terminal entrances at Lagos's Murtala Muhammed Airport and Abuja's Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport from the early hours.

Air Peace, Enugu Air, and United Nigeria Airlines all suspended or rescheduled flights as a result, citing restricted access to their terminals. The unions say the action follows expired 14 day, 7 day, and 3 day ultimatums given to airlines over alleged anti-union practices, the casualisation of workers, and the non-remittance of over ₦25 billion in statutory Ticket Sales Charges (TSC), a 5% levy collected from passengers that airlines are required to pass on to the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

TUC President Festus Osifo confirmed the union's backing for the action at a press briefing in Abuja, demanding the outstanding funds be remitted. The NCAA has appealed to the unions for a peaceful resolution. As of the latest reports, affected airlines were advising passengers to check for rebooking updates before heading to the airport.

ayra-starr-starrgirl-third-album.html.title: Ayra Starr Releases Third Studio Album ‘Starrgirl’
ayra-starr-starrgirl-third-album.html.excerpt: Grammy-nominated Afrobeats star Ayra Starr has released her third studio album, “Starrgirl” — a 16-track project featuring Wizkid, Rema, ZAYN and Leon Thomas.
paras: Grammy-nominated Nigerian Afrobeats star Ayra Starr has released her third studio album, “Starrgirl,” via Mavin Records and Republic Records. The 16-track project arrived on Friday, August 14, 2026, and features collaborations with Wizkid, Rema, ZAYN, Leon Thomas and others.

Following her acclaimed 2024 album “The Year I Turned 21,” the record blends Afropop, R&B and global pop, and has been described by critics as an affirmation of her place among Afrobeats’ leading talents. Built on pre-release singles including “Gimme Dat” featuring Wizkid and “Who’s Dat Girl” featuring Rema, the album — wrapped in a striking purple aesthetic with a Yoruba gele on its cover — explores themes of self-sovereignty, identity and growth.
The 24-year-old, born Oyinkansola Aderibigbe, called it “a highly personal milestone.”

benue-stolen-newborn-recovered-gboko.htm.title: Police Recover Stolen Newborn Baby in Benue, Arrest Suspects
benue-stolen-newborn-recovered-gboko.htm.excerpt: A newborn baby stolen from a hospital in Gboko, Benue State by a woman posing as a nurse has been recovered and reunited with his mother, with several suspects arrested.
paras: The Benue State Police Command has recovered a newborn baby boy allegedly stolen from a healthcare facility in Gboko Local Government Area shortly after his birth, and confirmed the arrest of several suspects in connection with the incident.

Police Public Relations Officer DSP Peter Aondongu said the baby was taken from his mother on Tuesday morning at the Family Healthcare Centre in Gboko by a woman who allegedly disguised herself as a nurse. According to witnesses, the newborn did not cry immediately after delivery, prompting a nurse on duty to intervene; once the baby responded normally, the mother and child were moved to a ward, where the impostor approached and asked to examine the baby again before taking him toward the labour room.

The theft triggered tension at the hospital, drawing family members and concerned residents to the facility before security operatives were deployed. Aondongu said the baby was recovered in the early hours of Thursday and reunited with his mother at the police "A" Division in Gboko, with some suspects transferred to the state police headquarters in Makurdi and others held locally. Investigators are working to determine whether those arrested are linked to other cases of missing children in the area.

boniface-leverkusen-comeback-goal-drough.title: Victor Boniface Ends 16-Month Goal Drought With Pre-Season Brace as Leverkusen Comeback Continues
boniface-leverkusen-comeback-goal-drough.excerpt: Super Eagles striker Victor Boniface scored twice for Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season, ending a 16-month goal drought and continuing his injury comeback.
paras: Super Eagles striker Victor Boniface has ended a 16-month goal drought in dramatic fashion, scoring twice in four minutes as Bayer Leverkusen thrashed fifth-tier side Sportfreunde Baumberg 7-0 in a pre-season friendly, before following it up with further impressive performances in the weeks since.

It was Boniface's first goal for Leverkusen since March 2025, capping an injury-ravaged spell that included a difficult loan season at Werder Bremen, where he managed just 11 appearances and no goals. His market value has fallen sharply from around €40 million at its peak to roughly €5 million amid the fitness struggles, and two potential moves, to Saudi Arabia and to a Serie A club, both collapsed over concerns about his knee.
"Of course, I'm happy to be training again, playing again, and doing what I love again," Boniface said after the Baumberg match. "It's been a difficult year for me. It's a good feeling to be back."

New Leverkusen head coach Carles Martínez has been careful not to rush the 25-year-old, saying the priority remains rebuilding him physically before results. In a further pre-season outing against Kickers Offenbach, Boniface again impressed, this time in a creative role, setting up two goals in a 3-1 win. Sporting director Simon Rolfes described the striker's recent form as "an encouraging step" following what he called "a really difficult year overall," while stressing that more time is still needed before Boniface returns to his previous level. He remains under contract at Leverkusen until June 2028.

brentford-7-0-eintracht-frankfurt.html.title: Brentford Thrash Eintracht Frankfurt 7-0 in Pre-Season Rout
brentford-7-0-eintracht-frankfurt.html.excerpt: Brentford ended their pre-season campaign in style, hammering Bundesliga side Eintracht Frankfurt 7-0 ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League season.
paras: Brentford ended their pre-season campaign in emphatic fashion, hammering Bundesliga side Eintracht Frankfurt 7-0 at their training base on Saturday.
The result was one of the standout scorelines across a busy day of Premier League pre-season fixtures, with 13 top-flight clubs in action as teams wrapped up preparations for the 2026-27 season.
Brentford's dominant display offers an encouraging final send-off before their competitive campaign begins the week of August 21.

burna-boy-big-2-declaration.html.title: Burna Boy: "There's No Big 3 — Just the Big 2, and Then Me"
burna-boy-big-2-declaration.html.excerpt: Burna Boy has stirred fresh conversation online after distancing himself from the long-running "Big 3" tag shared with Davido and Wizkid.
burna-boy-big-2-declaration.html.caption: Burna Boy performing live. Photo: “Burna Boy (cropped)” via Wikimedia Commons, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0.
paras: Burna Boy has stirred fresh conversation across Nigerian social media after distancing himself from the long-running "Big 3" tag that groups him with Davido and Wizkid as the country's biggest music stars.

Speaking during a live performance, the Grammy-winning singer told the crowd there was no such thing as a "Big 3" — only a "Big 2," made up of Davido and Wizkid, with Burna Boy standing apart from both. "Next time anybody tells you about the 'Big 3,' tell them there's only the 'Big 2' — and then there's Burna Boy," he said, drawing loud cheers from the crowd.

The clip has circulated widely online, reigniting a debate that has followed Nigerian Afrobeats fandoms for years: who really sits at the top of the industry. Supporters of Wizkid and Davido pushed back online, while Burna Boy's fanbase — known as the Outsiders — embraced the line as further proof of his self-assurance.
It isn't the first time Burna Boy has positioned himself outside the "Big 3" framing; he's made similar claims before about his standing relative to his two most talked-about peers.
Whether the comment settles anything is unlikely — if anything, it's added fresh fuel to one of Afrobeats' most enduring arguments.

The "Big 3" label has followed Nigerian Afrobeats for years, used informally by fans and commentators to describe Wizkid, Davido, and Burna Boy as the genre's most commercially dominant, internationally recognised acts — each having headlined major arenas and stadiums across the UK, US, and Europe.

Comparisons between the three resurface almost every time one of them hits a new commercial milestone, whether a chart position, an award nomination, or a streaming record, with rival fanbases routinely citing the numbers as proof of supremacy. Burna Boy's comment is likely to feed that same cycle, rather than settle it.

burna-boy-shakira-world-cup-song-nominat.title: Burna Boy Earns Two Nominations for FIFA World Cup Song With Shakira
burna-boy-shakira-world-cup-song-nominat.excerpt: Nigerian star Burna Boy has received two nominations for “Dai Dai,” his collaboration with Shakira on the official 2026 FIFA World Cup song.
paras: Nigerian Afrobeats star Burna Boy has received two nominations for his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira on the official 2026 FIFA World Cup song, “Dai Dai.”
The recognition adds to a strong run for the Grammy-winning artist and highlights the growing global footprint of Afrobeats on major international stages.

carrick-confirms-rashford-stays-man-unit.title: Carrick Confirms Rashford Will Stay at Man United, Says Forward "Has Come Back Great"
carrick-confirms-rashford-stays-man-unit.excerpt: Michael Carrick has confirmed Marcus Rashford will remain at Manchester United this season, ending speculation about his future after a loan spell at Barcelona.
paras: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has confirmed that Marcus Rashford will remain at Old Trafford this season, ending speculation about the forward's future after a loan spell away from the club.

"He's our player, and he's come back great," Carrick told ITV Sport after United's pre-season win over Leeds, settled on penalties following a 1-1 draw. "He's just like any other player. I've known Marcus a long time, and he gives us something a little bit different."

United had reportedly hoped to sell Rashford permanently through a £26 million option built into his loan move to Barcelona, but the Catalan club chose not to activate it, instead signing Anthony Gordon from Newcastle. That left the 28-year-old, who still has two years remaining on his £325,000-a-week contract, back at Old Trafford with his future uncertain.

"He has been in great spirits since he's been back... it's pretty normal, to be honest," Carrick said, adding that Rashford was expected to feature alongside Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martínez in United's final pre-season fixture against AC Milan. Rashford was left out of the squad for the Leeds match but could make his first Manchester United appearance since December 2024 this coming weekend.

cbn-omo-liquidity-market-outlook.html.title: Analysts See Stronger Market as CBN Reviews OMO and Eases Liquidity Access
cbn-omo-liquidity-market-outlook.html.excerpt: Analysts expect a stronger equities market as the Central Bank reviews its Open Market Operations and eases access to liquidity.
paras: Analysts expect the Nigerian equities market to strengthen as the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) reviews its Open Market Operations (OMO) framework and eases access to liquidity, according to reports.
The expectation comes amid a recent multi-session correction on the Nigerian Exchange, with observers suggesting improved liquidity conditions could support renewed buying interest.

cbn-warns-rejection-standard-n100-note.h.title: CBN Warns Against Rejection of Standard N100 Note, Threatens Sanctions
cbn-warns-rejection-standard-n100-note.h.excerpt: The Central Bank of Nigeria has warned businesses and individuals against rejecting the standard N100 banknote, saying both it and the commemorative N100 note remain legal tender.
paras: The Central Bank of Nigeria has warned individuals, businesses, and financial institutions against rejecting the standard N100 banknote, saying offenders risk sanctions for violating the law and undermining confidence in the national currency.

The warning followed reports that some members of the public and businesses were refusing to accept the standard N100 note over confusion about its continued legal-tender status, apparently mixing it up with the commemorative N100 note issued to mark Nigeria's centenary. "For the avoidance of doubt, the CBN hereby reiterates that both the commemorative N100 banknote and the standard N100 banknote remain legal tender," the apex bank said in a statement issued by acting director of corporate communications Hakama Sidi Ali.

"Such rejection constitutes a violation of the provisions of the CBN Act and undermines confidence in the national currency. The Bank will not hesitate to apply appropriate enforcement measures against any person or entity found to be in breach," the statement added, urging Nigerians to continue accepting and transacting with all banknotes legally issued by the CBN.

champions-league-2026-27-draw-real-madri.title: Champions League Draw: Real Madrid to Face Arsenal, PSG Drawn Against Barcelona
champions-league-2026-27-draw-real-madri.excerpt: The 2026-27 Champions League league-phase draw in Monaco has paired Real Madrid against Arsenal and Inter Milan, while two-time reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain will face Barcelona and Manchester City.
paras: The draw for the league phase of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League was held on Thursday, August 27, 2026, in Monaco, revealing the opponents for all 36 teams in the competition’s primary stage.

Two-time reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain, chasing an unprecedented third straight title, will face Barcelona and Manchester City among their eight league-phase opponents. Fifteen-time winners Real Madrid were drawn against Arsenal and Inter Milan. From the Premier League, Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool have all qualified for the league phase.

The first round of matches will be played from September 8-10, 2026, running through eight matchdays until January 27, 2027, before the knockout stage. The final will be held at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid on Saturday, June 5, 2027.

chelsea-3-1-real-sociedad-xabi-alonso-de.title: Chelsea Beat Real Sociedad 3-1 in Xabi Alonso's First Match as Manager
chelsea-3-1-real-sociedad-xabi-alonso-de.excerpt: Chelsea began the Xabi Alonso era with a 3-1 pre-season win over Real Sociedad, with new signing Morgan Rogers scoring and Joao Pedro adding two second-half goals.
paras: Chelsea began the Xabi Alonso era with a 3-1 pre-season win over Real Sociedad, with new signing Morgan Rogers opening the scoring and Joao Pedro adding two second-half goals.

The £117 million signing Rogers tapped in the opener before Joao Pedro took over, extending his pre-season tally to seven goals in the tournament with a second-half brace at Stamford Bridge. The result gives Alonso, who replaces the previous coaching setup, a winning start ahead of the new Premier League campaign.
Chelsea were among 13 top-flight sides in pre-season action Saturday as clubs wrapped up preparations for the 2026-27 season, which begins August 21.

chelsea-transfer-spending-premier-league.title: Chelsea's Big-Spending Summer: 11 Signings Worth Over €400m
chelsea-transfer-spending-premier-league.excerpt: Chelsea have spent over €400m this summer, the most of any club in world football, as Xabi Alonso reshapes his squad with 11 new signings.
paras: Chelsea have emerged as the biggest spenders in world football this summer, completing 11 signings worth a combined total of more than €400 million as Xabi Alonso reshapes his squad ahead of the new season, according to the latest transfer figures from Europe's top five leagues.

Among the incoming names are Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson, two experienced Premier League figures brought in to add depth and leadership to Chelsea's young squad. The club's spending spree comes as the 2026 summer transfer window enters its final three weeks, with clubs across Europe racing to complete business before deadline day.

Chelsea's rivals have also been active. Tottenham Hotspur, under new manager Roberto De Zerbi, have spent heavily, bringing in Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, and Jan Paul van Hecke for a combined fee north of €260 million, while adding free transfers Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi, and Martin Dubravka. Arch-rivals Arsenal, meanwhile, have moved to defend their Premier League title with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapié, and goalkeeper Illan Meslier.
With the summer window closing across Europe's top leagues on September 1, further high-profile moves are expected before clubs finalise their squads for the 2026-27 season.

chris-brown-rihanna-testimony-dog-attack.title: Chris Brown Contests $13M Dog-Attack Verdict Over Rihanna Testimony
chris-brown-rihanna-testimony-dog-attack.excerpt: Chris Brown is seeking a new trial in a $12.9 million dog-attack judgment, arguing that testimony about his 2009 assault of Rihanna unfairly influenced the jury.
paras: Chris Brown is seeking to overturn a $12.9 million judgment against him in a former housekeeper's dog-attack lawsuit, arguing that the jury's verdict was influenced by testimony about his 2009 assault of then-girlfriend Rihanna.

Brown's lawyers filed a motion arguing that the singer's 2009 felony domestic violence conviction, raised during cross-examination when he was asked about prior convictions, had no bearing on the case and unfairly prejudiced the jury. The lawsuit was brought by Maria Avila, a former housekeeper who was seriously injured after a 200-pound guard dog attacked her at Brown's Los Angeles-area home in December 2020.

Avila's attorney, Nancy Doumanian, told Billboard she expects the request to be denied. "You can't hit the reset button every time a jury holds you accountable. The evidence was overwhelming, the jury got it right," she said. Brown had previously accepted some responsibility for the incident but disputed the size of the award, and his legal team is continuing to fight collection efforts on the judgment.

colombia-earthquake-death-toll.html.title: Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Passes 265, Still Rising
colombia-earthquake-death-toll.html.excerpt: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake in western Colombia has killed at least 265 people, injured thousands more, and left over 4,100 reported missing.
paras: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake that struck the Chocó region of western Colombia on August 10 has killed at least 265 people, injured more than 3,700 others, and left over 4,100 reported missing, according to the latest tallies as search and rescue operations continue.

The quake, Colombia's strongest in recent decades, caused extensive damage across Cali, Pereira, Quibdó, and Manizales, collapsing roughly 1,600 buildings including the towers of a historic cathedral in Manizales. Colombia's newly inaugurated president, Abelardo de la Espriella, declared a state of national disaster and has personally led emergency response efforts just days into his term.

Rescue crews have continued pulling survivors from rubble more than 30 hours after the initial quake, including a dramatic rescue of a baby in Cali. More than 70 aftershocks have been recorded since the initial tremor, complicating recovery efforts in some of the country's hardest-to-reach regions.
International leaders across the US, South America, Europe, and the Middle East have pledged support for ongoing rescue operations, as authorities warn the death toll is likely to continue rising.

congo-ebola-outbreak-2000-deaths.html.title: Congo Ebola Death Toll Passes 2,000 in Fastest-Growing Outbreak on Record
congo-ebola-outbreak-2000-deaths.html.excerpt: More than 2,000 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak, which is spreading faster than any recorded outbreak in history and is now the second-largest ever.
paras: More than 2,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak since it was declared in May, making it the fastest-growing outbreak on record and the second-largest in history, behind only the devastating 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic.

Government data showed 4,381 confirmed cases and 2,011 deaths as of this week, with roughly half of those deaths occurring in just the last three weeks. Health authorities believe the outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus, actually began in February, months before it was officially declared in mid-May. The outbreak has a case fatality rate of 45.9%, higher than the 39.6% recorded during the 2014-2016 outbreak, as care is not reaching many patients in time.

The response has been complicated by conflict in eastern Congo between the Congolese military and the Rwanda-backed M23 militia, alongside poor roads and disputes over health worker pay in remote areas. There is currently no approved vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain, though the World Health Organization says vaccine trials are underway, with results likely still months away. The UN reports more than 300 children have died in the outbreak so far.

creative-industry-next-oil-lai-mohammed..title: Nigeria's Creative Industry Is the Country's "Next Oil," Says Lai Mohammed
creative-industry-next-oil-lai-mohammed..excerpt: NIPSS and the Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy are partnering on a summit aimed at unlocking the sector's role in Nigeria's $1 trillion economic target.
paras: Former Minister of Information and Culture Lai Mohammed has described Nigeria's creative industry as the country's "next oil," as the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS) partners with the Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy to help drive President Bola Tinubu's target of a $1 trillion economy by 2030.

"I have always said it when I was a minister that our next oil is actually the creative industry — it's our films, music, gastronomy, fashion, publishing, sports," Mohammed said, noting the sector is Nigeria's second-largest employer of labour after agriculture.

The partnership centers on an upcoming National Summit and Exhibition on the Orange Economy, organised by NIPSS to bring together stakeholders and develop strategies for unlocking the sector's economic potential. NIPSS Director-General Prof. Ayo Omotayo said the institute had deliberately aligned its research agenda with the president's economic goals, describing the creative sector as "the last of the sectors" it identified as having enough leverage to meaningfully push Nigeria toward the trillion-dollar target.

Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy Hanatu Musawa said the ministry was deliberately repositioning the sector as an engine of economic growth under the government's Renewed Hope Agenda. Omotayo added that despite its potential, the creative industry has historically received limited policy research attention — something the summit is intended to help correct.

cristian-romero-tottenham-atletico-madri.title: Cristian Romero Completes €40m Move From Tottenham to Atlético Madrid
cristian-romero-tottenham-atletico-madri.excerpt: Argentina defender Cristian Romero has completed a €40 million move from Tottenham Hotspur to Atlético Madrid, as the summer transfer window enters its final weeks.
paras: Argentina international defender Cristian Romero has completed a permanent move from Tottenham Hotspur to Atlético Madrid in a deal worth €40 million, one of several confirmed transfers around Europe on Saturday.

Romero becomes Atlético's latest defensive addition as the Spanish side strengthens its backline ahead of the new La Liga season, which kicked off the same day. The centre-back had been a regular fixture for Tottenham since joining from Atalanta in 2021, and was part of Argentina's squad at the 2026 World Cup.

The move comes as Europe's top clubs continue major summer business ahead of the September 1 transfer deadline. Elsewhere on deadline-adjacent business, Real Madrid have added Marc Cucurella, Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konté, and Bernardo Silva this summer following José Mourinho's return to the club, while cross-town rivals Atlético continue reshaping their squad under a similarly ambitious rebuilding plan.

dangote-refinery-free-fuel-delivery-expa.title: Dangote Refinery Expands Free Fuel Delivery to Kano, Imo, Anambra, Nasarawa
dangote-refinery-free-fuel-delivery-expa.excerpt: Dangote Refinery has expanded its free petroleum product delivery initiative to Kano, Imo, Anambra and Nasarawa states, aiming to cut distribution costs and create room for lower pump prices.
paras: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has expanded its free petroleum product delivery initiative to Kano, Imo, Anambra and Nasarawa states, in a move expected to reduce distribution costs for independent marketers and create room for lower petrol prices at the pump.

The initiative, which began with deliveries to Lagos, Ogun, Rivers, Kaduna, Delta and the Federal Capital Territory, is designed to bring products closer to marketers and retailers while removing the cost of transporting fuel over long distances. By absorbing the delivery cost, the refinery is removing one of the key expenses built into the downstream distribution chain.

Group Executive Director, Commercial Operations, Fatima Aliko Dangote, said the aim was to ensure the benefits of domestic refining flow through to businesses and consumers beyond the refinery gate. Independent marketers, through IPMAN spokesman Chinedu Ukadike, welcomed the move and urged the refinery to extend it to more locations, particularly across northern Nigeria, describing it as “the beauty of deregulation and competition.” The refinery has a stated capacity of 650,000 barrels per day.

dangote-refinery-not-enough-africa-fuel-.title: Dangote Refinery Alone Can't Meet Africa's Fuel Needs, Says FG
dangote-refinery-not-enough-africa-fuel-.excerpt: The Federal Government is urging fresh investment in Nigeria's refining sector, saying the Dangote Refinery cannot single-handedly satisfy Africa's growing demand for refined fuel.
paras: The Federal Government has said the Dangote Petroleum Refinery cannot single-handedly meet Africa's growing demand for refined petroleum products, urging local and international investors to pour more capital into Nigeria's refining, midstream, and downstream sectors.

Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Heineken Lokpobiri, speaking at the second West Africa Refined Fuel Market Conference in Abuja, said Nigeria must build on the refinery's success and attract additional investment to become a major refined-fuel hub for the continent, not just West Africa. "The Dangote Refinery is not enough. Despite the fact that the refinery is increasing its refining capacity to 1.4 million barrels, it is not enough for the African continent," he said.

Lokpobiri cited rising European demand for the refinery's jet fuel as evidence of how interconnected the global petroleum market has become, saying it demonstrated the need to deepen domestic refining capacity and develop responsive pricing structures. He assured stakeholders the government would continue supporting the development of a regional petroleum market and the institutions needed to sustain it.

davido-1m-bet-most-hits-afrobeats.html.title: Davido Offers $1 Million Bet, Insists ‘Nobody Has More Hits Than Me’
davido-1m-bet-most-hits-afrobeats.html.excerpt: The Afrobeats star reignited debate over his standing in the genre, publicly challenging anyone to match his hit record for a $1 million wager.
paras: Afrobeats superstar David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has stirred fresh conversation online after offering a $1 million bet to anyone who can challenge his record of hit songs, insisting nobody in the genre has more.

The remark quickly circulated across Nigerian social media, reigniting a long-running debate among fans about who sits at the top of the Afrobeats industry — a discussion that frequently pits Davido against peers Wizkid and Burna Boy.

davido-only-artist-number-one-every-year.title: Davido Becomes Only Artist With a No.1 Nigerian Single Every Year Since Chart Tracking Began
davido-only-artist-number-one-every-year.excerpt: Davido has extended a record no other Nigerian artist has matched: at least one No.1 single on TurnTable Charts' Official Nigeria Top 100 every year since 2020.
paras: Afrobeats star Davido has extended a record no other Nigerian artist has matched: at least one No.1 single on TurnTable Charts' Official Nigeria Top 100 in every calendar year since the chart's tracking began in 2020.

The streak started with "FEM," which became an anthem during Nigeria's #EndSARS protests in 2020 and gave Davido his first chart-topper. He has followed it every year since, most recently with "With You" featuring Omah Lay, which debuted at No.1 this year off his fifth studio album, "5ive." The song marked his eleventh career No.1 in Nigeria, a tally bettered only by Asake's twelve.

"5ive" has already produced three No.1 singles on its own, including "Awuke" featuring YG Marley and "Funds" featuring Odumodublvck and Chike, matching a feat achieved by only a handful of albums in the chart's history. The consistency stands out in an industry where even the biggest stars typically go multiple years without topping the chart at all.
The milestone comes as Davido continues his "5 Alive" world tour, which includes a headlining show at London's 60,000-capacity Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

davido-trump-osun-election.html.title: Davido Appeals to Trump Over Osun Election Violence Fears
davido-trump-osun-election.html.excerpt: Afrobeats star Davido has asked US President Trump and the international community to monitor Nigeria's Osun State governorship election amid fears of violence.
paras: Afrobeats star Davido, born David Adeleke, has publicly appealed to United States President Donald Trump and the international community to closely monitor Nigeria's upcoming Osun State governorship election, citing concerns about possible violence and voter intimidation ahead of the August 15 vote.

In a statement posted to his official X account, Davido addressed Trump directly, asking that voters be protected and that the process remain credible. He said Osun residents deserve to vote "freely, peacefully, and without fear," adding that he wants "peace, transparency, and a free and fair election" rather than bloodshed or intimidation.

The appeal comes with a personal stake attached: Davido's uncle, incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, is seeking re-election on the Accord Party ticket, and the singer has been actively involved in youth campaign mobilisation on his behalf.

Davido had earlier signalled the move during a livestream with content creator Carter Efe, saying he would seek Trump's intervention and take his concerns to the White House if the election were manipulated.

Reaction online has been mixed. Some supported his call for international attention, while others questioned why a foreign head of state's involvement was being sought in a domestic Nigerian election. Responding to one such challenge, Davido noted that he holds dual citizenship.

The governorship election itself is a closely watched contest. Governor Ademola Adeleke is seeking a second term on the Accord Party platform, facing challengers from the APC and PDP in a race that has drawn national attention in part because of his nephew's high profile. Osun has a history of tightly contested and occasionally disputed state elections, which has fed some of the anxiety around this year's vote.

Civil society and election-monitoring groups in Nigeria have separately called for a heavier security presence around polling units in the state ahead of August 15, citing isolated incidents of unrest in past cycles. As of publication, there has been no public response from the Trump administration or the U.S. State Department to Davido's appeal.

The Trump appeal wasn't Davido's only intervention in the race. Days earlier, he had also appealed directly to Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma — chairman of the APC's Osun campaign council — urging him not to interfere in the election. An aide to Uzodimma dismissed that appeal as "emotional blackmail," a remark the governor later distanced himself from, saying he had not authorised the response. Uzodimma said he would still attend campaign events in Osun in support of the APC candidate, adding, "Davido remains my son," but that his presence there would not make him an eligible voter in the state.

The Trump post itself drew a mixed reaction online, with some users mocking Davido for appealing to a foreign head of state over a Nigerian election. When one asked, "Is everything okay, David?", Davido shot back, "So I can't tweet my president again?" — a reference to his dual Nigerian and American citizenship; he was born in Atlanta before being raised in Lagos.

Adeleke faces a crowded field in the August 15 vote, including the APC's Bola Oyebamiji and the African Democratic Congress candidate, Najeem Salaam, in what's widely regarded as one of the most closely watched state elections of the year.

dhq-x-account-hacked-crypto-posts.html.title: Defence Headquarters' X Account Hacked, Flooded With Crypto Posts
dhq-x-account-hacked-crypto-posts.html.excerpt: The Defence Headquarters says its official X account has been compromised and flooded with cryptocurrency posts, warning the public to disregard content until it regains control.
paras: The Defence Headquarters says its official X (formerly Twitter) account has been compromised, warning the public to disregard any content posted from the account until it regains full control.

Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba, said the incident, discovered Saturday, is being treated as a cybersecurity matter, with technical measures already activated to secure the account. A Premium Times check found the account, which has more than 980,000 followers and still carries its verification badge and military gallery, had been flooded with cryptocurrency-related posts unrelated to the armed forces.

The DHQ urged the public to rely instead on its verified Facebook page ("Defence Headquarters Nigeria"), Instagram (@defenceheadquarters), and WhatsApp channel for accurate updates while efforts continue to restore the account. The breach is notable given the account's role as one of the military's primary channels for announcing combat operations and other official updates.

diddy-released-solitary-confinement-pris.title: Diddy Released From Solitary Confinement Following Alleged Prison Fight
diddy-released-solitary-confinement-pris.excerpt: Sean "Diddy" Combs is back in the general prison population at FCI Fort Dix after weeks in solitary confinement following a reported altercation with another inmate.
paras: Sean "Diddy" Combs is back in the general population at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey after spending several weeks in solitary confinement following a reported altercation with another inmate in July.

According to multiple reports citing sources close to the situation, the fight began after another inmate made a disrespectful comment toward Combs, escalating into pushing and punches before correctional officers intervened and separated the two men. Combs was moved to the prison's Special Housing Unit while officials reviewed the incident.

The Federal Bureau of Prisons has declined to comment on the matter, citing its standard policy of not discussing individual inmate disciplinary matters. Combs is serving a 50-month sentence after being convicted last year on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution, a conviction he is appealing. His projected release date is currently set for February 2028.

doku-man-city-contract-reijnders-sale.ht.title: Doku Signs New Man City Deal Until 2031 as Reijnders Set to Depart
doku-man-city-contract-reijnders-sale.ht.excerpt: Jérémy Doku has signed a new five-year Manchester City contract until 2031, as the club closes in on selling midfielder Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah for around £51m.
paras: Manchester City winger Jérémy Doku has signed a new five-year contract, extending his stay at the Etihad until 2031, as the club also closes in on selling midfielder Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi club Al-Qadsiah.

Doku's previous deal had been due to expire in 2028, but City moved to secure the Belgian winger's long-term future after he emerged as one of the club's most important attacking players since joining from Rennes in 2023. He has made 131 appearances for City, scoring 22 goals and providing 29 assists, and was part of Belgium's run to the World Cup quarter-finals this summer.

"This club means so much to me," Doku said. "I feel their love and support, and it means the world to me." City Director of Football Hugo Viana praised the 24-year-old's growth since joining, calling him "a fantastic person" who is "loved across the club." Doku becomes the fourth City player to commit to a long-term extension this summer, following Phil Foden, Josko Gvardiol, and Abdukodir Khusanov.
Meanwhile, City are separately negotiating the sale of midfielder Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah for a fee in the region of £51 million, a year after signing him from AC Milan for £46.5m.

dr-congo-ebola-5000-cases-deadliest.html.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Passes 5,000 Cases, Becomes Deadliest in Country’s History
dr-congo-ebola-5000-cases-deadliest.html.excerpt: The WHO says the Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has passed 5,000 cases and killed more than 2,300 people — the deadliest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record.
paras: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has passed 5,000 confirmed cases and become the deadliest in the country’s history, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned, describing it as a continuing global health emergency.

Government data showed the outbreak had recorded 5,021 cases, including 2,378 deaths, as of mid-August 2026 — infecting and killing people faster than any previous Ebola outbreak on record. The epidemic, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a strain for which existing Ebola vaccines and treatments were not originally certified, began in Ituri Province in May 2026 and has since spread to more than 50 health zones across six provinces.

Following an emergency meeting, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on the international community to help contain the outbreak, warning that the epidemic was far from being under control. Response efforts have been strained by remote terrain, insecurity, and reports of unpaid health workers going on strike.

dss-releases-marwana-oyo-compensation.ht.title: DSS Releases Carpenter Wrongly Linked to Oyo School Abduction, Pays ₦3m Compensation
dss-releases-marwana-oyo-compensation.ht.excerpt: Mustapha Marwana was cleared of any link to a terrorist group after a DSS panel found no evidence connecting him to the May attack on three Oyo schools.
paras: The Department of State Services has released Mustapha Marwana, a carpenter from Katsina State, after an internal investigation cleared him of any connection to the abduction and killing of pupils and teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State.

Marwana had been detained over suspected links to Ansaru, the terrorist group blamed for the May 15 attack on three schools in the Ogbomoso axis of Oyo State — Community Grammar School, Baptist Nursery/Primary School, and L.A. Primary School — in which 39 pupils and seven teachers were abducted. Two victims, including a teacher, were killed before the remaining captives were freed on July 10 following a military operation.

A DSS panel reviewing the case found no evidence linking Marwana to the group's membership, financing, logistics, or operations. Following the review, DSS Director-General Oluwatosin Ajayi ordered his immediate release and approved an initial ₦3 million compensation payment to help him meet his immediate needs and restart his livelihood. He was handed over to his lawyer.

A security source said the DSS has made similar payments in other cases of mistaken identity, citing an October 2025 case in which an Abuja businesswoman wrongfully arrested over suspected oil bunkering received ₦10 million in compensation after her release. Several suspects linked to the Oriire attack have already been arraigned before the Federal High Court in Abuja, with three sentenced to life imprisonment after pleading guilty.

ederson-manchester-united-medical.html.title: Man United's Éderson Deal Collapses Over Failed Medical
ederson-manchester-united-medical.html.excerpt: Manchester United's £39m deal for Atalanta midfielder Éderson has fallen through after he failed a medical, though the club hasn't fully ruled out reviving the move later in the window.
paras: Manchester United's move for Atalanta midfielder Éderson has collapsed after the Brazilian failed a medical, ending, for now, what would have been the club's first major signing of the summer.

United had agreed a fee of £35 million plus £4 million in add-ons with Atalanta, and Éderson had completed the first phase of his medical while away with Brazil at the 2026 World Cup. But after further examination, United chose not to proceed with the paperwork. Atalanta said the player is fully fit and ready to return, and their new sporting director Cristiano Giuntoli said the club were "stunned" the move broke down.

United have denied the deal is completely off, and Sky Sports reports the club may revisit signing Éderson later in the transfer window, though not at the original price and structure. In the meantime, United have turned their attention elsewhere, completing a £50m signing of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and closing in on Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa.

edo-okpebholo-4800-special-assistants.ht.title: Edo Governor Okpebholo Appoints 4,800 Special Assistants Across 192 Wards
edo-okpebholo-4800-special-assistants.ht.excerpt: Edo Governor Monday Okpebholo has approved 4,800 Special Assistants across the state's 192 wards, with 25 SAs per ward, sparking debate over the scale of the appointments.
paras: Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo has approved the appointment of 4,800 Special Assistants across the state's 192 wards, with 25 SAs allocated to each ward, sparking debate online over the scale of the appointments.

Okpebholo announced the move at a meeting with APC members from the state's 18 local government areas at the Government House in Benin City, describing it as part of efforts to take governance to the grassroots. "Appointing 4,000 SAs is not an issue at all because we all worked for this victory. The victory does not belong to Okpebholo alone," he said.

Edo APC Chairman Jarret Tenebe said the state's ruling party working committee had set up a process to engage with wards, ensure compliance with selection guidelines, and compile the names of qualified nominees before submitting them to party headquarters, suggesting the appointments are still at the selection stage rather than finalized. The announcement has drawn mixed reactions, with some questioning the cost and scale of the appointments given past comparisons — former Governor Godwin Obaseki had 186 senior special assistants and advisers during his tenure.

efcc-icpc-probe-nff-12bn-fund.html.title: EFCC, ICPC Probe ₦12bn Federal Government Intervention Fund Released to NFF
efcc-icpc-probe-nff-12bn-fund.html.excerpt: Nigeria’s two anti-graft agencies are investigating how the Nigeria Football Federation used a ₦12bn FG intervention fund meant to clear players’ wages and bonuses, after the NFF cited the probe in declining an FOI request.
paras: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) are investigating the utilisation of a ₦12 billion Federal Government intervention fund released to the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) to settle outstanding players’ wages, allowances and bonuses.

The investigation became public after the NFF, in a letter dated August 18, 2026 (reference NFF/LEG/10/1/879, signed by Onoja Joshua on behalf of the General Secretary), declined a Freedom of Information request for the fund’s financial records and utilisation logs, stating that all relevant documents were already with the EFCC and ICPC.

The ₦12 billion was approved by President Bola Tinubu in January 2024 to clear obligations to the national teams, including up to 15 months of unpaid salaries owed to Super Eagles coaches, plus allowances for the men’s and women’s senior teams and the U-20 side. The probe comes amid intense scrutiny of Nigerian football following the Super Eagles’ failure to qualify for the 2026 World Cup and the Super Falcons’ failure to reach the 2027 Women’s World Cup, with the Senate Committee on Sports also summoning NFF and National Sports Commission officials. No wrongdoing has been established.

efcc-probes-kano-airport-currency-seizur.title: EFCC Probes Suspect After Customs Seizes $73,000 and Other Currencies at Kano Airport
efcc-probes-kano-airport-currency-seizur.excerpt: The anti-graft agency has opened an investigation after Customs intercepted large sums of undeclared foreign currency concealed in luggage at Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport.
paras: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has commenced an investigation into a suspect, Haruna Yusuf, after the Nigeria Customs Service intercepted undeclared foreign currencies worth $73,000, £15,957 and 827,800 Saudi Riyals at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport (MAKIA).

According to the Customs Service, the money was seized in two separate operations during routine screening of arriving passengers between August 8 and 12, 2026. In the first, officers reportedly found unaccompanied luggage containing 827,800 Saudi Riyals and $53,300 concealed in footwear. In the second, officers allegedly found $20,000 and £15,957 hidden in sports shoes.

The suspect and recovered funds were handed over to the EFCC’s Kano Zonal Directorate by Acting Customs Area Comptroller U.U. Adamu, who cited the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023. The EFCC said the matter remains under investigation, with possible prosecution to follow. The suspect has not been convicted of any offence.

efcc-recovers-n115bn-nddc-levies.html.title: EFCC Recovers N115bn in NDDC Levies From Oil Companies
efcc-recovers-n115bn-nddc-levies.html.excerpt: The EFCC has recovered over N115 billion and $81 million in unpaid statutory levies owed the Niger Delta Development Commission by 24 oil companies, clearing 19 others of liability.
paras: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has recovered more than N115 billion and $81 million in outstanding statutory levies owed to the Niger Delta Development Commission by oil companies operating between 2021 and 2023.

EFCC representative Francis Oka-Phillips Usani told the Senate Committee on Public Accounts that the commission investigated 43 oil companies following findings in the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative's 2021-2023 Oil and Gas Sector Audit Report. Of these, 24 companies operating in the Niger Delta were found to have outstanding liabilities totalling N76.883 billion and $81.076 million in unpaid three percent statutory levies, while the remaining 19 were cleared.

Usani said N73.373 billion and $67.070 million recovered on the NDDC's behalf had already been released to the commission, with N3.510 billion and $14.005 million still held in the EFCC's recovery account. The Senate committee separately rejected an attempt by TotalEnergies EP Nigeria to respond to audit queries through inadequate representation, directing the company's managing director to appear in person the following week.

enterprise-life-assurance-raises-capital.title: Enterprise Life Assurance Raises Paid-Up Capital to Over N18.7bn
enterprise-life-assurance-raises-capital.excerpt: Enterprise Life Assurance Nigeria has raised its paid-up share capital to over N18.7 billion, nearly double the regulatory minimum, positioning it to underwrite larger risks.
paras: Enterprise Life Assurance Nigeria Limited has raised its paid-up share capital to over N18.7 billion, significantly exceeding the N10 billion regulatory minimum set by the National Insurance Commission for life insurers under the industry's recapitalisation framework.

The milestone was marked in Abuja, where NAICOM presented the company's Managing Director and CEO, Nelson Akerele, with a new operational licence. Akerele said the additional capital would enable Enterprise Life to write larger risks, expand into new markets, and accelerate technology-led insurance offerings targeted at Nigeria's underinsured middle-class and mass-market segments. "This milestone reflects our ambition to build one of Nigeria's most trusted and innovative life insurance companies," he said.

The capital raise was independently verified by PricewaterhouseCoopers. The stronger balance sheet gives the insurer operational headroom that analysts say few of its peers can currently match, as Nigerian insurers continue racing to meet recapitalisation deadlines under the industry's reform framework.

enugu-police-arrest-12-kidnappers-ransom.title: Enugu Police Arrest 12 Kidnappers Who Allegedly Killed Female Victim After Collecting Ransom
enugu-police-arrest-12-kidnappers-ransom.excerpt: Police in Enugu State say they have arrested 12 kidnappers who allegedly collected large ransoms and then killed a female victim.
paras: The police in Enugu State say they have arrested 12 suspected kidnappers who allegedly collected ransoms — reported at $98,700 and ₦30.5 million — and then killed a female victim.

The Commissioner of Police in Enugu State, Bitrus Giwa, disclosed this during a press briefing and parade of the suspects at the State Police Headquarters. He said the suspects were arrested through intelligence-led operations conducted across several states, including the FCT, Enugu, Kogi, Nasarawa, Rivers, Kwara and Taraba, on various dates in June, July and August 2026.
None of the suspects has been convicted of any offence; investigations are continuing.

fadahunsi-police-questioning-kill-accord.title: Police Question Senator Fadahunsi Over Viral "Kill Accord" Remark Ahead of Osun Election
fadahunsi-police-questioning-kill-accord.excerpt: Senator Francis Fadahunsi was questioned by Osun police for nearly two hours over a viral video in which he appeared to tell supporters to "kill" Accord Party members. He was released without charge.
paras: Osun State Police interrogated Senator Francis Fadahunsi, representing Osun East, for nearly two hours on Wednesday over a viral video in which he appeared to tell APC supporters to "kill" members of the rival Accord Party, two days before Saturday's closely contested governorship election.

The video, recorded at a protest at the palace of the Owa Obokun of Ijesaland in Ilesa, showed Fadahunsi addressing supporters in Yoruba following reports that a dozen APC members had been killed in the area within 24 hours. Police summoned him in a letter dated August 11, signed by the Commissioner of Police for Elections, Samuel Etaifo Erale, describing his remarks as "threatening, inciting and intimidating."

Fadahunsi's team pushed back on the video's interpretation, issuing a statement titled "Kill Osun Accord with Votes, Not Violence," saying the senator's actual message was a call for supporters to defeat the Accord Party at the ballot box through lawful, peaceful means, not a literal call to violence. Governor Ademola Adeleke, who is seeking re-election on the Accord Party platform, had earlier demanded Fadahunsi's arrest over the video.

Fadahunsi was released after questioning without being charged. He said afterward that he intended to pursue legal action against those he accused of distorting the video's meaning. The episode adds to a tense run-up to Saturday's election, with both camps accusing each other of violence against supporters in the weeks before the vote.
