fayose-obi-adc-exit-2027-chances.html.title: Fayose Says Obi’s Exit From ADC Weakened Opposition’s 2027 Chances
fayose-obi-adc-exit-2027-chances.html.excerpt: Former Ekiti Governor Ayodele Fayose says Peter Obi’s decision to leave the ADC effectively ended his 2027 presidential chances and handed Tinubu an advantage.
paras: Former Ekiti State Governor Ayodele Fayose has said Peter Obi’s decision to leave the African Democratic Congress (ADC) effectively ended his chances of winning the 2027 presidential election.

According to Fayose, Obi and other opposition politicians weakened their collective chances against the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) through disunity, which he said has handed President Bola Tinubu an advantage ahead of the vote.

fg-automates-civil-service-postings-ippi.title: FG Automates Civil Service Postings and Promotions With New IPPIS Modules
fg-automates-civil-service-postings-ippi.excerpt: The Federal Government has launched IPPIS Human Resource Modules to digitise postings, promotions, and leave applications across 508 federal MDAs.
paras: The Federal Government has launched the Human Resource Modules of the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System (IPPIS), introducing a fully digital platform to automate staff postings, promotions, leave applications, and other personnel processes across the Federal Civil Service.

Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Mrs Didi Esther Walson-Jack, said at the IPPIS Go-Live Ceremony in Abuja that the platform marks a major milestone in building a modern, technology-driven public service. "We are not just unveiling a digital platform, but institutionalising a better way of managing our most important resource, which is our people, our employees," she said.

The platform, developed by SoftAlliance and Resources Limited, now covers 508 MDAs and more than one million employee records, expanding IPPIS from a payroll system into a comprehensive human capital management solution covering recruitment, onboarding, promotions, transfers, and workforce analytics.

fifa-sacks-lamour-world-cup-sale.html.title: FIFA Sacks Top Executive Who Criticised Infantino’s World Cup Sale Plan
fifa-sacks-lamour-world-cup-sale.html.excerpt: Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour has left FIFA weeks after publicly attacking President Gianni Infantino’s now-abandoned plan to sell World Cup stakes to private investors.
paras: FIFA has parted ways with its Chief Operating Officer, Kevin Lamour, weeks after he publicly criticised President Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell a stake in the governing body’s tournament business — including the World Cup — to outside investors.

“FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA’s Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026,” a FIFA spokesperson said, thanking him for his service and declining further comment.

Lamour had told the Associated Press in late July that FIFA staff felt “deceived” over the plan, describing it as “the project of one person.” His comments came shortly after senior Infantino adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned in protest, calling the proposal “a bad deal for football.”

The now-scrapped plan sought to create a roughly $20 billion FIFA subsidiary and sell up to a 20% stake to external investors. It triggered fierce backlash from bodies including UEFA, which threatened to boycott FIFA competitions, prompting FIFA to withdraw the proposal.

first-lady-food-bank-ogun-launch.html.title: First Lady Oluremi Tinubu Leads Zonal Launch of National Food Bank Programme in Ogun
first-lady-food-bank-ogun-launch.html.excerpt: Nigeria’s First Lady headlined the South-West zonal launch of the National Community Food Bank Programme in Ogun State, distributing food to vulnerable residents and commissioning several projects.
paras: Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, led governors, First Ladies and other dignitaries to Ogun State for the zonal launch of the National Community Food Bank Programme, which distributes food items to vulnerable and indigent residents. The programme commenced at Makun, Sagamu.

According to a statement by the Special Adviser to the Ogun State Governor on Information and Strategy, Kayode Akinmade, Mrs Tinubu also commissioned the 108-unit Muhammadu Buhari Estate at Kobape, Abeokuta, and the Gateway Medical Centre of Excellence, a 250-bed hospital in Abeokuta.

The initiative is part of the Federal Government’s social intervention efforts. The broader programme targets 500,000 vulnerable households nationwide in its first year, focusing on children under six, and pregnant and lactating mothers.

fubara-backs-chinda-rivers-successor.htm.title: Fubara Backs Kingsley Chinda as Preferred Rivers Successor
fubara-backs-chinda-rivers-successor.htm.excerpt: Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara has publicly endorsed APC candidate Kingsley Chinda as his preferred successor, following reconciliation with predecessor Nyesom Wike.
paras: Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara has publicly endorsed Kingsley Chinda, governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, as his preferred successor, declaring his support for the Rainbow Coalition backed by FCT Minister Nyesom Wike.

Speaking at the commissioning of the Rivers Medical Industries Project in Port Harcourt, Fubara said, "We have made peace in the state, and we have a total agreement. I am supporting our rainbow party, our Rainbow Coalition. President Bola Tinubu is our president, and he is the one we are supporting."

Fubara had initially been screened alongside Chinda for the APC governorship primary before withdrawing, citing a commitment to peace and unity in the state. The endorsement marks a significant turning point after a prolonged political feud between Fubara and Wike that had triggered impeachment efforts against the governor before both camps reached a truce.

goodness-ekunke-chess-champion.html.title: 14-Year-Old Nigerian Wins Inaugural World Amateur Rapid Chess Championship
goodness-ekunke-chess-champion.html.excerpt: Goodness Ekunke, 14, beat a field of far more experienced players to win the first-ever FIDE World Amateur Rapid Chess Championship in Abuja.
paras: Nigeria has a new global chess champion — and he's only 14 years old. Goodness Ekunke, known in local chess circles as "Boss Baby," won the inaugural FIDE World Amateur Rapid Chess Championship in Abuja, finishing the 11-round tournament with 9 points out of a possible 11.

The Bayelsa-born teenager beat back a strong international field that included far more experienced players, several of them senior FIDE-titled masters. Two fellow Nigerians, FM Eugene Unwana and FM Bomo Kigigha, took second and third place, each finishing on 8½ points — meaning Nigerian players swept the podium.

The tournament had late drama. Seventeen-year-old Joseph Sambo briefly seized control of the standings in the eighth round after upsetting Ekunke, then knocked out Kigigha and Unwana in later rounds before his own challenge faded, leaving him fourth. Unwana surged back with wins over Kigigha and Sambo to close the gap, setting up a winner-takes-all final round against Ekunke. The two Nigerians fought to a draw — enough for Ekunke to hold on and claim the historic title.

Organised jointly by FIDE and the Nigeria Chess Federation, the championship was played with a 15-minute time control and a 10-second increment per move. Ekunke, who became Nigeria's national Under-14 champion at just eight years old, is now being talked about as a future Grandmaster prospect — a milestone only a handful of Sub-Saharan African players have ever reached.

The win adds to a period of steady growth for chess in Nigeria, with federal and state-level programmes increasingly investing in school chess clubs, youth coaching, and international tournament exposure for promising young players. Ekunke himself has been coached within that same pipeline, having progressed from national age-group titles to senior international competition in the space of a few years.

Should he continue his trajectory toward the Grandmaster title, Ekunke would become just the sixth player from Sub-Saharan Africa to hold it — a reflection of how rare, and how significant, this week's result is for Nigerian chess.

icpc-indicts-budget-office-fake-agency.h.title: ICPC Indicts Budget Office Over Inclusion of Fake Agency in 2026 Budget
icpc-indicts-budget-office-fake-agency.h.excerpt: The ICPC has indicted the Budget Office of the Federation over the inclusion of a fictitious agency in the 2026 national budget, deepening a widening scandal over fake agencies embedded in government structures.
paras: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has indicted the Budget Office of the Federation over the inclusion of a fictitious agency in the 2026 national budget, deepening a widening scandal over fake agencies embedded in government structures.

The finding follows the ICPC’s earlier uncovering of bogus offices operating within the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, which led President Tinubu to order the arrest of a fake-agency promoter and suspend three permanent secretaries.

The commission said it would continue to review budgetary line items across ministries, departments and agencies to identify further irregularities linked to non-existent or unauthorised offices. No wrongdoing has been established against any named individual at this stage.

igp-disu-washington-cpc-meeting.html.title: IGP Disu Attends US-Nigeria Security Talks in Washington, Highlights Police Reform Efforts
igp-disu-washington-cpc-meeting.html.excerpt: Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu represented Nigeria at the second US-Nigeria CPC Joint Working Group meeting in Washington, D.C.
paras: Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Rilwan Disu represented the Nigeria Police Force at the second meeting of the United States-Nigeria Country of Particular Concern (CPC) Joint Working Group, held in Washington, D.C. on August 12.

The working group was established after the U.S. redesignated Nigeria as a "Country of Particular Concern" over religious freedom concerns, creating a formal channel for both countries to discuss counter-terrorism cooperation, religious freedom, and human rights. Wednesday's session followed the group's inaugural meeting, held in Abuja in January, and reviewed progress made against the group's roadmap for the April-to-June reporting period.

Disu was part of a Nigerian delegation that included the National Security Adviser, the Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Interior, and Defence, service chiefs, and heads of other security agencies. Presenting the police force's contributions, Disu highlighted sustained counter-kidnapping and anti-banditry operations, expanded police presence in vulnerable communities, and measures supporting the safe return of internally displaced persons.

He also disclosed that the recruitment of 50,000 new police constables is nearing its final pre-training stage, with preparations underway for a training curriculum based on international best practices. Disu reaffirmed the force's commitment to lawful, professional investigations and civilian protection, framing the police force's work as part of Nigeria's broader counterterrorism and rule-of-law objectives.

indonesia-earthquake-flores-island-death.title: Indonesia Earthquake: Death Toll Passes 47 After 7.7-Magnitude Quake Hits Flores Island
indonesia-earthquake-flores-island-death.excerpt: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off Indonesia's Flores Island, killing at least 47 people and triggering a tsunami warning that was later lifted.
paras: A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores Island early Saturday, killing at least 47 people, destroying homes, and triggering a tsunami warning that was later lifted.

The US Geological Survey said the quake struck at 5:58am local time, with its epicentre about 68 kilometres north-northwest of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province. More than 230 aftershocks followed, the strongest measuring magnitude 6.2, while a separate magnitude 6.9 quake also struck Indonesia's Sumatra island later the same day.

Officials said the quake flattened at least 157 houses, damaged nearly 200 more, and destroyed over 100 public facilities including schools and medical centres, forcing roughly 2,000 people to flee to temporary shelters. Search and rescue efforts have been hampered by landslides that blocked roads and cut off remote villages. Indonesia sits on the Pacific "Ring of Fire" and is one of the world's most seismically active nations; the same coastline was struck by a similarly powerful quake in 1992 that killed more than 2,500 people.

inec-osun-ballot-reprint-sdp-candidate.h.title: INEC Reprints Osun Ballot Papers to Include SDP Candidate Ahead of Saturday's Election
inec-osun-ballot-reprint-sdp-candidate.h.excerpt: INEC has begun reprinting Osun governorship ballot papers to include SDP candidate Dr. Francis Ajala, days before Saturday's closely watched election.
paras: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has begun reprinting ballot papers and result sheets for Saturday's Osun State governorship election to include the Social Democratic Party (SDP) candidate, Dr. Francis Olugbenga Ajala, and his running mate, Faseke Babajimi Oladipo.

The move comes just days before the election, adding a late but notable development to an already closely watched race. Osun's governorship contest features incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party seeking re-election against a crowded field, including the APC's Bola Oyebamiji and the ADC's Najeem Salaam.

The election has drawn heightened national attention in the run-up to Saturday's vote, with civil society groups and the Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) raising concerns about rising political tension in the state. The Nigerian Bar Association has separately called on police to maintain neutrality and prevent political violence ahead of the poll, while European Union-backed civil society groups have engaged directly with the Inspector-General of Police on election security arrangements.

INEC has not indicated whether the late addition of the SDP candidate will affect the distribution timeline for ballot materials, but the commission is expected to complete the reprinting process before polling units open on Saturday.

inec-osun-pvc-centre-attack-wont-disrupt.title: INEC Says Attack on Osun PVC Centre Won't Disrupt Governorship Poll
inec-osun-pvc-centre-attack-wont-disrupt.excerpt: INEC says a gun attack on a PVC collection centre in Osun State's Odo-Otin LGA will not derail preparations for Saturday's governorship election.
paras: The Independent National Electoral Commission says an attack on one of its Permanent Voter Card collection centres in Osun State will not deter it from conducting a free, fair, and credible governorship election on Saturday.

Police said about ten armed hoodlums stormed the Oyinlola DC Primary School collection centre in Okuku, Odo-Otin Local Government Area, firing shots into the air before making away with three packs of PVCs and reportedly carting off Bimodal Voter Accreditation System devices.

INEC's Chief Press Secretary, Dayo Oketola, said the incident had been reported to police and was under investigation, but stressed it would not affect the commission's preparations. "INEC cannot be distracted. We will conduct a free and fair election in Osun," he said, adding that 4,427 BVAS devices, including 664 backup units, had been configured for the election, and that no registered voter would be disenfranchised over stolen PVCs.

iran-rejects-trump-hormuz-territory-clai.title: Iran Rejects Trump's "Delusions" Over Claim to Strait of Hormuz
iran-rejects-trump-hormuz-territory-clai.excerpt: Iran has firmly rejected Trump's suggestion he could declare the Strait of Hormuz US territory, as a ceasefire deadline over the critical waterway approaches Monday.
paras: Iran has firmly rejected US President Donald Trump's suggestion that he could soon declare the Strait of Hormuz "a territory of the United States," calling the claim delusional as tensions over the critical waterway remain high.

Speaking in New York on Friday, Trump said, "After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States." Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi responded on X: "The Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian. This strait will only be closed and opened under Iran's command," adding that it "cannot be seized with a tweet, nor with an aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order, nor through an election speech."

The strait, which normally carries around a fifth of the world's seaborne oil trade, has been a central flashpoint since the US and Israel began striking Iran in late February. Iran has restricted traffic through the waterway and continued targeting vessels it associates with US interests, while Washington maintains its own naval blockade. A ceasefire memorandum agreed in June included a 60-day window set to expire Monday, making the coming days a significant test of whether diplomacy can hold.

islamic-new-year-hijri-holiday-2026.html.title: Federal Government to Announce Islamic New Year Public Holiday
islamic-new-year-hijri-holiday-2026.html.excerpt: The Federal Government is set to announce the public holiday to mark the Islamic New Year, with a list of observances expected.
paras: The Federal Government is expected to announce the public holiday to mark the Islamic New Year (Hijri 1448), as Nigerians await the official declaration.
Islamic New Year is observed nationally, and the government typically issues a formal statement confirming the holiday date.

iswap-finance-operative-surrenders-borno.title: Alleged Senior ISWAP Finance Operative Surrenders to Troops in Borno
iswap-finance-operative-surrenders-borno.excerpt: Musa Usman, an alleged senior ISWAP finance operative, surrendered to troops of Operation Hadin Kai in Borno State, arriving with his two young sons.
paras: Musa Usman, an alleged senior finance operative of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), has surrendered to troops of Operation Hadin Kai in Borno State, arriving with his two sons, aged 10 and 15.

Acting military information officer Captain Mohammed Goni said the 40-year-old surrendered to troops of 3 Battalion along the Ladari-Jegarawa-Tunokalia axis, amid a wave of roughly 46 terrorists and family members voluntarily laying down arms in recent days.

Preliminary profiling identified Usman as the chief finance operative of an ISWAP enclave at Jubillaram, responsible for overseeing financial operations and logistics. Troops recovered an AK-47 rifle, four magazines, 101 rounds of ammunition, a motorcycle, and cash from him. He and his children are undergoing further profiling and interrogation.

jowizaza-father-freed-kidnappers-anambra.title: Jowizaza's Father, Billionaire Joseph Ezeokafor, Freed After 11 Days in Kidnappers' Custody
jowizaza-father-freed-kidnappers-anambra.excerpt: Chief Joseph Ezeokafor, father of socialite Jowizaza, has been freed after 11 days in kidnappers' custody in Anambra, with a ransom reportedly demanded of up to N1.5 billion.
paras: Chief Joseph Ebere Ezeokafor, chairman of the Jezco Group of Companies and father of Nigerian socialite Jowizaza, has regained his freedom after 11 days in captivity, the Anambra State Police Command confirmed Saturday.

Ezeokafor was abducted on August 4 while travelling to a prayer ground in the Ifite-Awka area of Anambra's state capital. A Catholic reverend sister taken alongside him was also released and returned safely. Police spokesperson SP Tochukwu Ikenga said the command is now working to establish the circumstances of their release and gather information to track down the perpetrators, with Commissioner of Police Nnanna Oji Ama directing a joint manhunt involving the police, military, DSS, and NSCDC.

According to family accounts, the kidnappers initially demanded ₦700 million before raising the ransom to ₦1.5 billion during negotiations; police have not confirmed whether any payment was made. Jowizaza broke his silence on Instagram following his father's release, sharing a post set to gospel music that drew an outpouring of relief from fellow celebrities including Obi Cubana and Cubana Chiefpriest. Ezeokafor, 1980 founder of Jezco Oil and Lubricants, built the company into a broader manufacturing and commercial enterprise over four decades.

kaduna-vc-rebuts-asuu-resignation.html.title: Kaduna University VC Accuses ASUU of Misrepresenting Facts on Mass Resignation
kaduna-vc-rebuts-asuu-resignation.html.excerpt: The Vice-Chancellor of Kaduna State University has accused ASUU of misrepresenting facts over the reported mass resignation of lecturers.
paras: The Vice-Chancellor of Kaduna State University (KASU) has accused the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) of misrepresenting facts regarding the reported mass resignation of more than 200 lecturers.

The response follows the union’s earlier claim that over 200 academics had resigned over poor pay and the non-implementation of the 2025 FG–ASUU agreement, and adds the university management’s side to the dispute.

kasu-200-lecturers-resign-asuu-strike.ht.title: Over 200 Lecturers Resign From Kaduna State University as ASUU Threatens Strike
kasu-200-lecturers-resign-asuu-strike.ht.excerpt: The union says more than 200 academics, including professors, have quit KASU over poor pay, and has issued a two-week ultimatum before a possible indefinite strike.
paras: More than 200 lecturers, including professors, have resigned from Kaduna State University (KASU) over poor conditions of service and the non-implementation of the 2025 Federal Government–ASUU agreement, the university’s ASUU chapter has said.

ASUU-KASU Chairman Dr Abubakar Abdullahi disclosed this at a press conference in Kaduna on Monday, warning that the union had issued a two-week ultimatum to the state government and university authorities to implement the agreement or face “a total, comprehensive and indefinite strike.”

Abdullahi said the 2025 agreement took effect in January 2026 but had yet to be implemented at KASU. He said most of the departed lecturers had secured jobs at newer universities, and blamed poor remuneration and declining welfare that had left KASU staff among the least-paid university workers in the country.
He warned that the exodus of experienced academics could damage teaching and research for years, and cautioned that continued delay would lead to accumulating salary arrears dating to January 2026.

katsina-dss-northwest-security-collabora.title: Katsina Governor, DSS Chief Call for Stronger North-West Security Collaboration
katsina-dss-northwest-security-collabora.excerpt: Katsina Governor Dikko Radda and DSS Director-General Oluwatosin Ajayi have called for stronger inter-agency collaboration to tackle terrorism and banditry across Nigeria's North-West.
paras: Katsina State Governor Dikko Radda and DSS Director-General Oluwatosin Ajayi have called for stronger collaboration among security agencies, government institutions, and communities to tackle terrorism and banditry across Nigeria's North-West.

The two spoke Thursday at the second North-West Zonal Conference of State Directors of Security in Katsina, themed "Unite Against Terror." Radda, represented by his deputy, Faruk Jobe, said the region's security challenges were interconnected and required a coordinated response, noting that about 26 local government areas in Katsina had faced constant attacks when his administration took office. He credited a mix of security operations and social interventions, including free medical care for banditry victims and agricultural support, with improving the situation.

Ajayi, represented by Kano State DSS Director Husseini Abubakar, said the DSS was strengthening its personnel's tactical capabilities to respond to emerging threats, and stressed the need for continued cooperation among security and law enforcement agencies. The conference was expected to produce a communique outlining measures on intelligence sharing, joint operations, and community engagement across the region.

katsina-police-foil-bandit-attack-fulala.title: Police Foil Bandit Attack, Rescue Kidnap Victims in Katsina
katsina-police-foil-bandit-attack-fulala.excerpt: The Katsina State Police Command foiled a bandit attack in Fulalawa village, Musawa LGA, rescuing several kidnap victims and recovering two motorcycles.
paras: The Katsina State Police Command has foiled an attack by suspected bandits in Fulalawa village, Musawa Local Government Area, rescuing several kidnapped residents and recovering two motorcycles.

Police spokesperson Abubakar Aliyu said the Musawa Police Division received a distress call reporting that armed bandits had attacked the village, breaking into shops, abducting residents, and rustling livestock. A joint security team was deployed to the scene, where the bandits opened fire on sighting the operatives. "The joint team responded with superior tactics and firepower, forcing the attackers to abandon their captives and flee into nearby bushes with suspected gunshot injuries," Aliyu said.

The rescued residents were reunited with their families following the operation. The incident is the latest in a string of coordinated security responses across Katsina State's North-West flashpoints, as police and community security groups continue joint operations against banditry and kidnapping in the region.

kebbi-police-killed-bandits-gun-battle.h.title: 10 Policemen, 2 Civilians Killed in Gun Battle With Bandits in Kebbi
kebbi-police-killed-bandits-gun-battle.h.excerpt: Ten police officers and two civilians were killed after bandits ambushed a checkpoint in Sakaba LGA, Kebbi State, in one of the deadliest attacks on security personnel this year.
paras: Ten police officers and two civilians were killed after a heavily armed group of bandits ambushed a police checkpoint in Sakaba Local Government Area of Kebbi State, in one of the deadliest single attacks on security personnel in the region this year.

The Nigeria Police Force said the incident occurred at about 9:25 a.m. on Monday, August 10, along the Rafin Makuku axis, when officers intercepted a large group of bandits moving between Zamfara and Kebbi states. Kebbi State Police Command spokesperson DSP Bashir Usman said the attackers had camped overnight in a forest between two communities before advancing toward Maburya, where they overpowered the checkpoint. Police say at least 17 suspected bandits were neutralised in the resulting gun battle, and four motorcycles belonging to the attackers were destroyed. Two other officers were injured and are receiving treatment.

The ten slain officers were named as ASP Bala Buba, and Inspectors Saminu Sulaiman, Solomon Jatau, Ayuba Hassain, Umar Yahuza, Auwal Sani, Adamu Abdullahi, and Abdullahi Magaji, along with Sergeant Jimoh Momo and Corporal Ukpong Otrukmj. Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu described their deaths as "a painful loss to the Force and the nation," saying they "paid the ultimate price while defending the people they swore to protect."

Reports indicate the bandits seized a number of rifles and other weapons from the fallen officers before fleeing. Security operations along the Zamfara-Kebbi border area are ongoing as authorities work to track down the remaining attackers.

kingibe-accuses-wike-abuja-floods.html.title: Senator Kingibe Accuses FCT Minister Wike of Worsening Abuja Floods
kingibe-accuses-wike-abuja-floods.html.excerpt: FCT Senator Ireti Kingibe has blamed the FCT Administration under Minister Nyesom Wike for worsening flooding in Abuja by allowing construction on green areas and flood channels.
paras: FCT Senator Ireti Kingibe has publicly criticised the Federal Capital Territory Administration under Minister Nyesom Wike, accusing it of worsening Abuja’s flooding problem by permitting building on green areas and flood channels.

According to the senator, development approvals that allow structures on designated green spaces and drainage channels have reduced the city’s capacity to manage heavy rainfall, contributing to flooding in parts of the capital.
The claims are the senator’s own; the FCT Administration has not been reported to have formally responded to the specific allegations.

kwara-ak47-procurement-arrest.html.title: Police Foil AK-47 Procurement Deal in Kwara, Arrest Buyer
kwara-ak47-procurement-arrest.html.excerpt: Police in Kwara State arrested a suspect, Sanda Aliyu, attempting to purchase an AK-47 rifle for ₦1.6 million.
paras: Police in Kwara State have arrested a suspect identified as Sanda Aliyu after he attempted to purchase an AK-47 rifle for ₦1.6 million, foiling the illegal arms procurement deal.

The arrest is part of ongoing efforts by the Kwara Police Command to intercept illegal weapons circulation in the state, with investigations continuing to trace the source of the firearm and identify any other individuals connected to the transaction.
Police in the state have stepped up operations against illegal arms trafficking in recent weeks amid broader national concern over weapons flowing into the hands of criminal and armed groups.

kwara-ilorin-tanker-petrol-spill-panic.h.title: Panic in Ilorin as 45,000 Litres of Petrol Spills From Tanker
kwara-ilorin-tanker-petrol-spill-panic.h.excerpt: Roughly 45,000 litres of petrol spilled from a tanker at an Ilorin filling station on Saturday, sparking panic before firefighters contained the hazard without casualties.
paras: Panic broke out in parts of Ilorin, Kwara State, on Saturday after roughly 45,000 litres of petrol spilled from a tanker at a filling station along Old Jebba Road, though firefighters contained the hazard without any reported casualties.

The Kwara State Fire Service said the incident occurred around 5:08pm at a Conoil station in the Maraba area, after station staff found a discrepancy between the tanker's expected and measured fuel quantity. An attempt to retrieve fuel from the tanker caused its valve to open, and the product began gushing out uncontrollably.

Fire Service spokesperson Hassan Adekunle said police and the state's road traffic authority helped control vehicular movement around the area, keeping motorists away while firefighters worked. He urged filling station operators and tanker owners to exercise greater caution during fuel loading, transport, and discharge, and to ensure valves and hoses are properly maintained.

lagos-lsstf-security-vehicles-donation.h.title: Firm Donates ₦300m Security Vehicles to Lagos Task Force
lagos-lsstf-security-vehicles-donation.h.excerpt: Lagos State's security architecture has received a boost following the donation of 10 operational vehicles worth over ₦300 million to the Lagos State Security Trust Fund.
paras: Lagos State's security architecture has received a significant boost following the donation of 10 operational vehicles, valued at more than ₦300 million, to the Lagos State Security Trust Fund (LSSTF).

The donation is intended to strengthen the operational capacity of security agencies across the state, supporting patrol and rapid-response efforts as part of ongoing efforts to improve public safety in Lagos.

The LSSTF has continued to serve as a channel for private-sector support of state security operations, with the latest donation adding to the fund's fleet of vehicles deployed to various security formations across the state.

lagos-warns-dealer-plates-175-vehicles.h.title: Lagos Warns Against Illegal Use of Dealer Plates, Impounds 175 Vehicles
lagos-warns-dealer-plates-175-vehicles.h.excerpt: The Lagos State Government says it has apprehended 175 vehicles in a crackdown on the misuse of dealer number plates, warning of impoundment and prosecution.
paras: The Lagos State Government has reiterated its prohibition on the permanent or everyday use of dealer number plates, warning motorists and dealers against deploying them outside their legally permitted purposes.

Under the Lagos State Transport Sector Reform Law, 2018, dealer plates are issued strictly for time-limited activities such as authorised test drives, vehicle inspections, delivery or collection of vehicles, and moving unregistered vehicles from ports or dealer premises to designated locations. Using them for private daily commuting or on already-sold vehicles awaiting registration is prohibited.

As part of enforcement, the state’s Vehicle Inspection Service apprehended 175 vehicles found in violation, the government said, adding that recovered dealer plates would be confiscated and the vehicles investigated. It warned that any vehicle using unauthorised, fake or obscured plates faces impoundment and prosecution, and urged full compliance for accountability and road safety.

luigi-mangione-guilty-plea-unitedhealthc.title: Luigi Mangione Pleads Guilty in Killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO
luigi-mangione-guilty-plea-unitedhealthc.excerpt: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to federal stalking charges in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, admitting he shot Thompson outside an investor conference in Manhattan.
paras: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty Friday in New York federal court to stalking UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson before fatally shooting him on a Midtown Manhattan street in December 2024, admitting for the first time in detail how he planned the killing.

In his allocution, Mangione said he emailed UnitedHealthcare posing as an investor managing more than $50 billion in assets to learn the exact location of the company's investor conference. "Before traveling to New York, I used a 3-D printer to make part of a gun, and I equipped the gun with the silencer and the magazine," he told the court. "My travel to New York and email to UnitedHealthcare was with the intent to shoot Brian Thompson... On the morning of Dec. 4, 2024, I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan and he died."

Manhattan U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said prosecutors will seek a life sentence on the charges of interstate stalking resulting in death and using electronic communications to stalk the CEO. Thompson's family, present in court, said in a statement that "today's guilty plea marks an important step toward justice for Brian and for our family." Mangione remains in federal custody pending sentencing, scheduled for December 18, and still faces separate murder charges in New York state court, which his lawyers are seeking to dismiss on double jeopardy grounds.

lukaku-farewell-napoli-message.html.title: Lukaku Bids Farewell to Napoli, Thanks Club for Career Revival
lukaku-farewell-napoli-message.html.excerpt: Romelu Lukaku has posted an emotional farewell message to Napoli, confirming his permanent departure after helping the club win the Serie A title.
paras: Romelu Lukaku has posted an emotional farewell message to Napoli fans, confirming his permanent departure from the club after a stint that included winning the Serie A title.

"Dear Napoli, thank you for making me feel at home! Thank you for believing in a moment where I was with my back against the wall," Lukaku wrote in an Instagram post. "We did amazing things and I will cherish them forever. Forza Napoli sempre."

The Belgian striker joined Napoli from Chelsea and became a key figure under manager Antonio Conte, helping the club win the 2024-25 Serie A title and finishing as the team's leading scorer that season. His final campaign was disrupted by a serious muscle injury sustained in pre-season, limiting him to just over 60 minutes of action before his departure was confirmed. Lukaku remains part of Belgium's squad for the 2026 World Cup.

makinde-picks-daura-apm-running-mate.htm.title: Makinde Picks Ex-DSS Chief Lawal Daura as APM Running Mate for 2027
makinde-picks-daura-apm-running-mate.htm.excerpt: Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde was elected APM presidential candidate at the party's Bauchi convention, naming former DSS DG Lawal Daura as his running mate for 2027.
paras: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde was formally elected presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) at the party's national convention in Bauchi on Thursday, naming former Department of State Services Director-General Lawal Musa Daura as his running mate for the 2027 election.

Daura, who led the DSS from 2015 to 2018 under the Buhari administration, replaces Ibrahim Adamu Bala, who had earlier been listed as a placeholder running mate on INEC's nomination portal. Makinde said Daura's intelligence background made him a deliberate choice to help address Nigeria's security challenges.

"As we approach 2027, the task before all of us is bigger than winning an election. It is to give Nigerians a real choice about the future of their country," Makinde told the convention. He called on Nigeria's opposition parties to work together to present a credible alternative in 2027, pledging to tackle insecurity and economic hardship if elected.

man-united-4-2-ac-milan-preseason-defeat.title: AC Milan Complete Stunning Comeback to Beat Man United 4-2 in Pre-Season Finale
man-united-4-2-ac-milan-preseason-defeat.excerpt: AC Milan came from behind twice to beat Manchester United 4-2 in Wroclaw, with Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu's goals wiped out by a second-half collapse.
paras: AC Milan staged a stunning second-half comeback to beat Manchester United 4-2 in their final pre-season friendly at the Tarczyński Arena in Wrocław, Poland, in a match that brought an intriguing reunion between Milan boss Ruben Amorim and his former club.

Harry Maguire headed United in front inside two minutes from a Bruno Fernandes corner, but Samuel Chukwueze equalised for Milan before half-time. United missed a golden chance to retake the lead when Fernandes had a penalty saved by Lorenzo Torriani. Patrick Dorgu restored United's advantage shortly after the break, capitalising on a Milan defensive error, but the Rossoneri responded emphatically: Alphonso Cissè levelled before Gonçalo Ramos and Ruben Loftus-Cheek struck within four minutes to complete the turnaround.

The result rounds off the pre-season for both clubs, with United, managed by Michael Carrick, having posted stronger warm-up results overall including wins over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid. Milan, by contrast, had failed to win any of their first three friendlies under new boss Amorim before finding their form against his old side. Both clubs now turn their attention to the start of their domestic league campaigns next week.

man-united-bruno-fernandes-contract-talk.title: Man United in Talks Over New Bruno Fernandes Contract as Galatasaray Circle
man-united-bruno-fernandes-contract-talk.excerpt: Manchester United have opened contract talks with captain Bruno Fernandes and hope to reach a deal soon, with the midfielder prioritising a stay despite outside interest.
paras: Manchester United are in talks over a new contract for club captain Bruno Fernandes, with the two sides working to reach an agreement soon.

The 31-year-old, whose current deal runs until 2027 with a one-year option, is central to Michael Carrick’s plans after an outstanding campaign in which he helped drive United’s Champions League qualification. A release clause reportedly set around €65m lapsed earlier this summer.

Galatasaray have been credited with long-standing interest — reportedly tabling a proposal for the Portugal international — alongside admirers in Saudi Arabia and Europe. But reporting indicates Fernandes is prioritising a stay at Old Trafford, and United have shown no interest in a sale.

manor-solomon-west-ham-transfer.html.title: Manor Solomon Completes Permanent Move to West Ham
manor-solomon-west-ham-transfer.html.excerpt: Manor Solomon has left Tottenham to join West Ham on a permanent deal worth up to £7m, following a successful loan spell in Florence.
paras: Manor Solomon has completed a permanent move from Tottenham Hotspur to West Ham United, ending his spell at the north London club after impressing on loan at Fiorentina last season.

The deal is worth £5 million in a fixed fee, with a further £2 million available in add-ons. Solomon has signed a three-year contract with West Ham, with the option of a further season, and will remain in London having previously done well on loan in Florence.
The winger becomes West Ham's latest addition as the club continues to reshape its squad ahead of the new Premier League season, adding attacking depth following a mixed campaign last term.

military-150-terrorists-surrender-northe.title: Military Says About 150 Terrorists Surrender as Pressure Mounts in North-East
military-150-terrorists-surrender-northe.excerpt: The Nigerian military says about 150 terrorists surrendered as sustained operations increase pressure on armed groups in the North-East.
paras: The Nigerian military has said that about 150 terrorists surrendered as sustained operational pressure mounts on armed groups in the North-East, according to reports.

The reported surrenders come amid intensified military operations across the region as security forces press ongoing campaigns against Boko Haram and ISWAP factions, part of a broader push to degrade insurgent capacity in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states.

military-terrorist-surrenders-213-percen.title: Terrorist Surrenders Rise 213% in North East in One Week, Military Says
military-terrorist-surrenders-213-percen.excerpt: The Nigerian military says terrorist surrenders in the North East rose 213 percent over the past week, driven by sustained ground operations under Operation HADIN KAI.
paras: The Nigerian military has recorded a 213 percent increase in the number of terrorist fighters and their associates surrendering to troops in the North East over the past week, in what officials describe as a sign of mounting pressure on insurgent groups.

The development follows sustained operations by troops of Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), combining coordinated ground actions, targeted engagements against identified terrorist positions, and efforts to disrupt terrorist logistics and supply routes across the theatre. Acting Military Information Officer, Captain Mohammed Goni, disclosed the figures in a statement issued Wednesday.

"During the period under review, the Theatre recorded a 213 percent increase in terrorist surrenders compared with the preceding week," Goni said, though the military did not release the specific number of surrenders behind the percentage. Two high-profile terrorist members reportedly surrendered with arms, ammunition, and other military equipment on Wednesday alone.

The Theatre Command said the surge reflects a "growing number of terrorist fighters and associates abandoning terrorist activities," attributing it to sustained military pressure that has weakened insurgents' operational capacity and cohesion. Operation HADIN KAI reaffirmed it would continue combining offensive operations with surrender channels for those willing to lay down arms, and urged members of the public to continue sharing credible information with security agencies.

mo-abudu-ebonylife-london-cinema.html.title: Mo Abudu Opens UK's First Cinema Dedicated to African Films
mo-abudu-ebonylife-london-cinema.html.excerpt: Media mogul Mo Abudu has unveiled EbonyLife Place in London, the UK's first cinema dedicated to African and Black films.
paras: Nigerian media mogul Mo Abudu has taken her EbonyLife Place brand to London, unveiling the United Kingdom's first cinema dedicated specifically to African and Black films.

The venue marks a significant expansion for EbonyLife, which has built a reputation as one of Africa's leading media and entertainment companies, and reflects growing international demand for African storytelling and Nollywood content.
The new London cinema is expected to give African filmmakers a dedicated platform to reach international audiences, further cementing the global reach of Nigerian and wider African cinema.

nafdac-recalls-sachet-alcohol-pet-bottle.title: NAFDAC Orders Recall and Destruction of Alcohol in Sachets and Small PET Bottles
nafdac-recalls-sachet-alcohol-pet-bottle.excerpt: NAFDAC has ordered the recall and destruction of alcoholic drinks packaged in sachets and small PET bottles, enforcing a long-planned phase-out aimed at curbing abuse and underage access.
paras: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has ordered the recall and destruction of alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and small-volume PET (polyethylene terephthalate) bottles, moving to enforce a long-planned phase-out.

NAFDAC Director-General, Professor Mojisola Adeyeye, said the measure targets the availability of cheap, easily concealed alcohol linked to abuse and underage consumption, with data showing a significant share of underage Nigerians have accessed alcohol through such packaging. The phase-out follows an earlier undertaking signed by distillers and marketers under the Distillers and Blenders Association of Nigeria (DIBAN).
The agency said it would work with manufacturers, distributors and state task forces to ensure compliance and remove non-compliant products from circulation nationwide.

naicom-revokes-universal-insurance-licen.title: NAICOM Revokes Universal Insurance Licence, Appoints Liquidator
naicom-revokes-universal-insurance-licen.excerpt: The National Insurance Commission has revoked the operating licence of Universal Insurance and appointed a liquidator.
paras: The National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) has revoked the operating licence of Universal Insurance and appointed a liquidator, according to reports.
The move is part of the regulator’s oversight of the insurance sector and its enforcement of solvency and operational standards.

naira-17-year-reserve-high-n1358.html.title: Naira Hits 17-Year Reserve High as Currency Strengthens to N1,358/$
naira-17-year-reserve-high-n1358.html.excerpt: The naira strengthened to N1,358.25/$ as Nigeria's external reserves climbed to $52.25 billion, their highest level in 17 years.
paras: The naira strengthened against the US dollar to close the week at N1,358.25/$1, as Nigeria's external reserves climbed to $52.25 billion, their highest level in 17 years.

Central Bank of Nigeria data showed the naira gained N5.75 over the week, appreciating 0.42% from the previous Friday's N1,364/$. The currency dipped mid-week to N1,365/$ on Tuesday before recovering over the final three trading sessions, closing at N1,360.15/$ Wednesday, N1,356.50/$ Thursday, and N1,358.25/$ Friday.

The rising reserves, up more than 28% from $40.72 billion a year earlier, strengthen the CBN's capacity to support the currency and meet the country's external obligations. In the parallel market, the naira held steady at N1,420/$, keeping the gap between official and black-market rates at a relatively narrow margin.

naira-dollar-exchange-rate-august-12.htm.title: Naira Holds Steady Against Dollar, Trading Around ₦1,364 Officially
naira-dollar-exchange-rate-august-12.htm.excerpt: The naira remained broadly stable on Wednesday, with the official rate around ₦1,364/$ and the parallel market holding in the low-₦1,400 range.
paras: The naira remained broadly stable against the US dollar on Wednesday, with the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) rate trading around the mid-₦1,360 band, while the parallel market held in the low-₦1,400 range.

Central Bank of Nigeria data put the official exchange rate at approximately ₦1,364 per dollar, a figure derived from the volume-weighted average of trades executed on the NFEM platform, and Nigeria's benchmark rate. Currency dealers in Lagos reported the parallel ("black") market trading at roughly ₦1,405 for buying and ₦1,415 for selling on Wednesday morning.

The spread between the official and parallel rates has remained relatively narrow in recent sessions, a contrast to the sharper gaps recorded through 2024 and early 2025. For Nigerians tracking rates for travel, school fees, imports, or international payments, the key levels to watch remain the ₦1,364/$ official window and the ₦1,415/$ parallel rate.

naira-firms-1350-dollar-strongest-april..title: Naira Firms to Around ₦1,350/$, Its Strongest Level Since April
naira-firms-1350-dollar-strongest-april..excerpt: The naira continued its recent appreciation, closing near ₦1,350 to the dollar at the official market — its best level in nearly four months.
paras: The naira traded firmly against the US dollar this week, extending recent gains at the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM). The currency closed at about ₦1,350 per dollar on Monday, August 17 — an appreciation of ₦8.25, or roughly 0.6%, from ₦1,358.25/$ on Friday, August 14.
According to Central Bank of Nigeria data, the Monday rate marked the naira’s strongest closing level since April 22, 2026. In early Tuesday trading, live rates put the dollar at around ₦1,352.

In the parallel market, the dollar was quoted at roughly ₦1,407 for buying and ₦1,420 for selling, based on the latest Bureau de Change rates. Analysts note parallel-market rates vary by location and dealer, while the official NFEM rate is a volume-weighted average of formal market transactions.

naira-five-month-high-1343-dollar.html.title: Naira Strengthens to Five-Month High Near ₦1,343/$ on Improved Dollar Supply
naira-five-month-high-1343-dollar.html.excerpt: The naira firmed to about ₦1,343 per dollar at the official market — its strongest level in roughly five months — as dollar liquidity improved.
paras: The naira continued to strengthen against the US dollar on Thursday, August 20, 2026, trading at about ₦1,344 at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) as improved dollar liquidity supported the local currency.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria showed the NFEM rate at ₦1,343.32 on August 18, after the currency closed around ₦1,350 on August 17. AbokiFX reported that the naira had risen to a five-month high of ₦1,343.32 at the official market. In the parallel market, the dollar sold for about ₦1,404 on Thursday.
The CBN says the NFEM rate is a volume-weighted average and serves as the official rate; actual rates vary by bank, Bureau de Change and transaction size.

napoli-badiashile-chelsea-loan-deal.html.title: Napoli Agree Deal to Sign Badiashile From Chelsea on Loan
napoli-badiashile-chelsea-loan-deal.html.excerpt: Napoli have agreed a loan deal with Chelsea for defender Benoît Badiashile, with an option to make the move permanent for €27 million next summer.
paras: Napoli have reached a verbal agreement with Chelsea to sign French defender Benoît Badiashile on loan, with an option to make the move permanent for €27 million next summer.

The deal sees Napoli pay an initial €3 million loan fee, with a further €1 million available in add-ons, while covering Badiashile's full salary during his time in Italy. Should Napoli activate the buy option at the end of the season, the total package could reach €31 million.

Badiashile joined Chelsea from Monaco in a near-€38 million deal in January 2023 but struggled to hold down a regular starting spot, particularly after Chelsea signed defender Maxence Lacroix. He is expected to complete the formalities before linking up with Napoli manager Massimiliano Allegri, who has been pushing to bring in defensive reinforcements after an injury crisis.

ncaa-rfid-baggage-tracking-airports.html.title: NCAA to Deploy RFID Technology to Curb Baggage Mishandling at Airports
ncaa-rfid-baggage-tracking-airports.html.excerpt: The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority plans to introduce RFID baggage tracking technology, letting passengers monitor checked luggage in real time from check-in to arrival.
paras: The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority has commenced moves to deploy Radio Frequency Identification technology at Nigerian airports to tackle persistent cases of lost, delayed, damaged, and misrouted passenger baggage.

NCAA Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Michael Achimugu, said baggage handling remains one of the industry's biggest sources of passenger complaints after flight delays. "For many years now, one of the biggest complaints in the industry has been that of baggage. Passengers frequently contend with bags that are short-landed, missing, lost or damaged," he said, noting the NCAA has met with domestic airlines, ground handlers, and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria to finalise plans for the migration.

The RFID system, which would replace the current barcode-based tracking technology, will allow passengers to monitor the location of their luggage through a mobile app from check-in until arrival at their destination. The NCAA is also reviewing existing regulations with a view to making automated baggage tracking mandatory for airlines operating in Nigeria, though it has not yet announced a timeline for the system going live.

ndlea-arrests-kc-luxury-cocaine-cartel.h.title: NDLEA Arrests Influencer ‘KC Luxury’ Over Alleged ₦39bn Cocaine Cartel as He Tried to Flee to Paris
ndlea-arrests-kc-luxury-cocaine-cartel.h.excerpt: The NDLEA says it has arrested Lagos socialite and influencer Afolabi Kazeem Michael, known online as “KC Luxury,” over his alleged role in an international cocaine syndicate, after intercepting a record 184.5kg cocaine consignment.
paras: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested Lagos socialite and social media influencer Afolabi Kazeem Michael, popularly known online as “KC Luxury,” over his alleged role in an international cocaine trafficking syndicate.

NDLEA Chairman Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.) announced the arrest at a press briefing in Lagos on Tuesday, August 18, 2026, describing the operation as one of the agency’s most significant narcotics investigations in recent times. According to the agency, the case began with the interception of 184.50 kilograms of cocaine concealed in a consignment being processed for export through a courier logistics company in Lagos — said to be the largest quantity of cocaine the NDLEA has ever intercepted through a courier company in the country.

The agency said Michael was apprehended on the night of August 13, 2026, at the boarding gate of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, as he allegedly attempted to board a business-class flight to Paris. The NDLEA said he was found with foreign currencies — €7,750, £2,800 and ₦100,000 — along with expensive jewellery, and that a search of his apartment on Banana Island, Ikoyi, recovered exotic vehicles.

Investigators alleged that Michael, who publicly presented himself as a businessman dealing in gold, jewellery and luxury goods, served as the cartel’s Nigerian “arrowhead,” and estimated the syndicate stood to earn as much as ₦39 billion from the shipment across a network spanning the UK, Europe and Asia. A logistics-firm employee, Lawal Mujab Kehinde, was also arrested in connection with the case. None of the suspects has been convicted of any offence.

ndlea-destroys-301bn-drugs-lagos.html.title: NDLEA Destroys Nearly 330,000kg of Illicit Drugs Worth ₦301 Billion in Lagos
ndlea-destroys-301bn-drugs-lagos.html.excerpt: The drug agency publicly destroyed a record haul of narcotics valued at over ₦301 billion in a court-ordered exercise at Navy Town, Ojo.
paras: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has publicly destroyed 329,865.585 kilograms of assorted illicit drugs with an estimated street value of ₦301.058 billion, in a court-ordered exercise at Navy Town, Ojo, Lagos, on Monday, August 17.

According to the agency, 246,864.535 kilograms were seized by its Lagos Strategic Command between April 2025 and May 2026, with the remaining 83,001.05 kilograms intercepted by the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Tincan, Apapa, Marine and special operations commands in Lagos.
The drugs included cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, several strains of cannabis, ephedrine, tramadol, codeine syrup, other opioids and khat leaves.

NDLEA Chairman Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.) described the destruction as a demonstration of Nigeria’s resolve to protect its people and starve criminal networks of resources. He said the exercise, ordered by the Federal High Court, disposed of drugs from concluded, uncontested cases and abandoned seizures, and linked drug trafficking to broader security threats including terrorism financing.

ndlea-lagos-drug-seizures-10bn.html.title: NDLEA Seizes N10bn Worth of Drugs in Lagos, Arrests Cocaine Kingpin
ndlea-lagos-drug-seizures-10bn.html.excerpt: The NDLEA intercepted cocaine, cannabis, and opioid consignments worth over N10 billion in a series of operations across Lagos ports and courier facilities.
paras: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency has intercepted a combined haul of cocaine, cannabis, and opioids worth an estimated N10 billion at Lagos ports and courier facilities, in operations conducted across a single week.

NDLEA spokesperson Femi Babafemi said the operations covered the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, the Apapa seaport, courier firms, and locations across Lagos, Katsina, and Edo states, combining intelligence-led airport and seaport interdictions with the unravelling of an organised cocaine export syndicate.

Among those arrested was 55-year-old businessman Onuigbo Ndubisi Chinedu, accused of masterminding an attempt to export cocaine to the United Kingdom through the Lagos airport. In a separate seizure, operatives recovered 2.24 million pills of Tapentadol valued at over N2.2 billion in cargo from India, while a raid in Edo State's Ilushi community produced over 1.2 tonnes of cannabis.

nff-committee-super-falcons-world-cup-fa.title: NFF Sets Up Committee to Investigate Super Falcons' World Cup Qualification Failure
nff-committee-super-falcons-world-cup-fa.excerpt: The NFF has constituted a fact-finding committee to investigate Nigeria's recent poor performances in international competitions, including the Super Falcons' World Cup qualification failure.
paras: The Nigeria Football Federation has constituted a fact-finding committee to investigate the country's recent poor performances in international competitions, with particular focus on the Super Falcons' failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup.

The decision follows Nigeria's exit at the WAFCON quarter-final stage and a subsequent 2-1 playoff defeat to South Africa that ended the Super Falcons' unbroken run of World Cup appearances dating back to the tournament's first edition in 1991. Ambassador Fanny Amun will chair the six-member committee, joined by former Flying Eagles coach Ladan Bosso, former Super Falcons captain Desire Oparanozie, former Super Eagles midfielder Mutiu Adepoju, and Dr Alex Mana, with Nasiru Jibril serving as secretary.

The NFF said the committee's mandate extends beyond the Super Falcons, taking in Nigeria's broader disappointing run across age-grade and senior competitions, including the Golden Eaglets missing the FIFA U-17 World Cup and the Flying Eagles failing to qualify for the FIFA U-20 World Cup.

ngx-seven-day-slide-5-trillion-loss.html.title: Nigerian Stocks Fall for Seventh Straight Session, Shedding About ₦5 Trillion in a Week
ngx-seven-day-slide-5-trillion-loss.html.excerpt: The Nigerian Exchange extended its correction for a seventh consecutive session on Wednesday, with market capitalisation down roughly ₦5 trillion over the seven-day slide.
paras: The Nigerian equities market extended its decline on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, with the All-Share Index (ASI) falling for a seventh consecutive session as selling pressure in oil and gas heavyweights — particularly Aradel Holdings — deepened the correction.

The ASI fell 0.36% to close at 240,750.47 points, down from 241,611.23 on Tuesday, while market capitalisation dropped about ₦555.68 billion to ₦155.42 trillion. Over the seven straight sessions from Tuesday, August 11, the index has shed about 3.13%, with market capitalisation falling roughly ₦5 trillion from ₦160.42 trillion on August 10 to ₦155.42 trillion.
Analysts noted the market remains firmly positive for the year, with a year-to-date return still above 54%, describing the pullback as a healthy correction after an earlier record rally.

ngx-stock-market-climbs-aug27.html.title: Nigerian Exchange Climbs as Market Capitalisation Adds ₦305bn
ngx-stock-market-climbs-aug27.html.excerpt: The Nigerian Exchange All-Share Index gained 473 points on Thursday, adding ₦305.56 billion to market capitalisation, as trading resumed after the Eid al-Mawlud holiday.
paras: The Nigerian Exchange (NGX) climbed on Thursday, August 27, 2026, as the All-Share Index added 473.17 points, or 0.20 per cent, to close at 239,156.09 points.

Market capitalisation rose by ₦305.56 billion to close at ₦154.44 trillion. Market breadth was negative despite the overall gain, with 22 stocks advancing, 40 declining and 85 closing unchanged. OMATEK led the gainers, rising 9.60 per cent to ₦1.37, followed by Cornerstone Insurance and Mansard, while Fidson paced the losers, shedding 9.98 per cent to close at ₦75.80.

Zenith Bank was the most actively traded stock by volume, with 69.95 million shares changing hands. Total volume for the session stood at 499.94 million shares, valued at ₦35.14 billion across 40,269 deals. The rebound followed a recent multi-session correction on the exchange.

ngx-stock-market-sheds-n1tn-bearish.html.title: Nigerian Stock Market Sheds N1.17tn as Bearish Trading Intensifies
ngx-stock-market-sheds-n1tn-bearish.html.excerpt: The domestic equities market closed lower as sell-offs in MTN Nigeria and 25 other stocks dragged the All-Share Index down 0.73%, wiping N1.17 trillion off market capitalisation.
paras: The Nigerian equities market closed on a bearish note as price depreciation in MTN Nigeria and 25 other stocks dragged overall market capitalisation lower by N1.17 trillion, ending a four-session winning streak.

The All-Share Index dropped 1,806.18 points, or 0.73 percent, to close at 246,723.57, while market capitalisation fell to N159.26 trillion from N160.42 trillion the previous session. The downturn was driven by profit-taking in large- and medium-capitalised stocks including MTN Nigeria, UACN, Dangote Sugar Refinery, Nigerian Aviation Handling Company, and First HoldCo. MTN Nigeria alone fell 4.73 percent, shedding N40 per share.

Despite the broader decline, market breadth closed positive with 27 gainers against 26 losers. FTN Cocoa led the gainers' chart, appreciating 9.88 percent, while Cadbury Nigeria stood out among blue-chip stocks, advancing 5.85 percent. The market's year-to-date return moderated to 58.55 percent from 59.71 percent as the correction pared back part of the gains from a record rally earlier in the week.

nhrc-355000-complaints-child-safety.html.title: NHRC Records Nearly 355,000 Complaints in July, Warns Over Child Sexual Violence
nhrc-355000-complaints-child-safety.html.excerpt: The National Human Rights Commission recorded 354,997 complaints in July and raised the alarm over child sexual violence and digital rights abuse.
paras: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) recorded 354,997 complaints in July 2026 and raised the alarm over rising child sexual violence and digital rights abuse, according to reports.
The figures underscore growing concern over the protection of children and citizens’ rights in Nigeria.

niger-state-troops-foil-terrorist-advanc.title: Troops Foil Terrorist Advance of 200 Motorcycles in Niger State
niger-state-troops-foil-terrorist-advanc.excerpt: Nigerian troops under Operation SAVANNAH SHIELD foiled an advance by terrorists riding roughly 200 motorcycles from Zamfara into Niger State.
paras: Troops of Operation SAVANNAH SHIELD have foiled an advance by terrorists riding an estimated 200 motorcycles from Zamfara State into Niger State, recovering an AK-47 rifle and 398 rounds of ammunition in the operation.

According to an operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria, the operation followed credible intelligence on the movement of the terrorists toward Inana Village in Rijau Local Government Area of Niger State. Troops of the 311 Army Reconnaissance Battalion, under 18 Brigade, engaged the terrorists at Majai and Tungan Bisallah villages.
The operation is the latest in a series of engagements as security forces continue to push back against armed groups operating across Nigeria's North-West and North-Central states.

nigeria-atu-chairmanship-abuja-declarati.title: Nigeria Assumes African Telecommunications Union Chairmanship
nigeria-atu-chairmanship-abuja-declarati.excerpt: Nigeria has assumed the chairmanship of the African Telecommunications Union's Conference of Plenipotentiaries, with member states adopting the Abuja Declaration on connectivity.
paras: Nigeria has assumed the chairmanship of the African Telecommunications Union (ATU) Conference of Plenipotentiaries, following the conclusion of the body's seventh ordinary session in Abuja.

Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy Minister Bosun Tijani assumed the role on Nigeria's behalf as the conference adopted the 2026 Abuja Declaration on Meaningful Connectivity for Africa, a framework prioritising broadband expansion, cybersecurity, and digital skills development across the continent.

The conference also saw Zambia's Kezias Kazuba Mwale elected as the ATU's next secretary-general after four rounds of voting, and elected 25 member states to serve on the union's Administrative Council for the next four years.

nigeria-fails-fiscal-transparency-test-2.title: Nigeria Fails US Fiscal Transparency Test for Second Consecutive Year
nigeria-fails-fiscal-transparency-test-2.excerpt: The US Department of State says Nigeria made no significant progress on fiscal transparency in 2025, placing it among 53 countries judged to have made no measurable improvement.
paras: Nigeria has failed to meet the United States government's minimum fiscal transparency requirements for the second consecutive year, according to the 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report released by the US Department of State.

The report assessed 139 governments and the Palestinian Authority, with only 73 meeting minimum standards. Of the 67 that fell short, 14 were judged to have made significant progress, while 53, including Nigeria, were marked as making no progress at all. The assessment was based on information gathered by the US Embassy in Abuja, federal agencies, international organisations, and civil society groups between January and December 2025.

The report faulted the executive branch for failing to publish its budget proposal before legislative approval, and comes amid domestic concern over budget implementation, with the Federal Government simultaneously managing the 2024, 2025, and 2026 budget cycles. The 2026 assessment also introduced a tougher requirement that governments publicly disclose the terms of sovereign loans, including liabilities and collateralised assets. In an initial reaction, the Presidency maintained that transparency and accountability remain a primary commitment of the administration.

nigeria-red-sea-tensions-oil-supply-warn.title: Nigeria Warns Red Sea Tensions May Disrupt Oil Supply, Maritime Trade
nigeria-red-sea-tensions-oil-supply-warn.excerpt: Nigeria's Federal Government has warned that escalating Red Sea hostilities could disrupt global oil supply and maritime trade, urging dialogue between parties.
paras: The Federal Government has expressed concern over escalating hostilities between Houthi forces in Yemen and Saudi Arabia, warning that disruption to navigation in the Red Sea could severely affect global oil supplies, maritime trade, and the wider world economy.

Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Kimiebi Ebienfa said Nigeria remains neutral in the conflict but urged all parties to embrace dialogue and diplomacy, noting that the tensions come amid unresolved disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict.

As a major oil-producing nation, Nigeria said it was particularly concerned that any blockade of the Bab al-Mandab Strait or sustained disruption to Red Sea shipping lanes would have direct consequences for global energy security. The government reaffirmed its sympathy with Saudi Arabia over attacks on its oil facilities and pledged support for international efforts to protect maritime infrastructure.

nigeria-startup-funding-crashes-96-perce.title: Nigerian Startup Funding Crashes 96% in July After June's $115m Surge
nigeria-startup-funding-crashes-96-perce.excerpt: Nigerian startups raised just $4.9 million in July, a 96% collapse from June's $115.2 million haul, as big investors pulled back sharply.
paras: Nigerian startups saw funding crash by 96 percent in July 2026, raising a combined $4.9 million across six disclosed deals, one of the country's weakest monthly funding performances in recent memory.

The collapse followed a strong June, when Nigerian startups raised $115.2 million across 18 deals, powered largely by Flutterwave's roughly $100 million Series E round from Ripple, which pushed the fintech unicorn's valuation to $3.2 billion. June funding also included climate and clean energy investments totalling $4.5 million from Lagos's Cascador Pitch Day.

July's funding was spread thinly across Education & Jobs, Agriculture & Food, and Deeptech startups, with investors largely backing early-stage ventures. Education technology startup Codar led the month with a $1.5 million seed round, matched by agritech startup Biochar Industrial Group's pre-seed raise of the same size. Compared to July 2025, when Nigerian startups raised $7.9 million, this year's figure still marks a year-on-year decline.

nigerian-army-repels-iswap-borno-base.ht.title: Nigerian Army Repels ISWAP Attack on Borno Military Base
nigerian-army-repels-iswap-borno-base.ht.excerpt: Troops of Operation HADIN KAI repelled a multi-pronged ISWAP attack on a Forward Operating Base in Mandaragirau, Borno State, in the early hours of Saturday.
paras: Troops of Operation HADIN KAI repelled a multi-pronged attack by ISWAP terrorists on a Forward Operating Base in Mandaragirau, Biu Local Government Area of Borno State, in the early hours of Saturday.

The attack began around 2am when terrorists simultaneously advanced on the base from two directions. According to Acting Military Information Officer Captain Muhammed Goni, troops detected the advance through early-warning and surveillance systems and deployed a combat team to intercept the attackers along one of their approach routes, triggering a heavy exchange of fire.

The terrorists suffered several casualties in the engagement, with none recorded on the Nigerian side. Troops recovered weapons, ammunition, and communication equipment from the scene. The military said further exploitation of the area was ongoing, and reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining pressure on ISWAP across the North-East.

nigerian-army-sscc-course-50-2027.html.title: Nigerian Army Opens Applications for Short Service Combatant Commission Course 50/2027
nigerian-army-sscc-course-50-2027.html.excerpt: The Nigerian Army has opened applications for its Short Service Combatant Commission Course 50/2027, open to qualified civilians and serving military personnel.
paras: The Nigerian Army has opened applications for its Short Service Combatant Commission (SSCC) Course 50/2027, inviting qualified civilians and serving military personnel to apply for commission as officers.

Successful candidates will undergo training before serving in the Army's Combat Arms, the Infantry and Armour Corps, or its Combat Support Arms, covering Artillery, Engineers, Signals, and Intelligence Corps. Applicants must be Nigerian citizens by birth, aged between 23 and 27 as of January 10, 2027, and meet the Army's medical, mental, and physical fitness standards.

The application portal opened on August 14 and closes October 17, 2026. Prospective applicants must apply through the official portal, nashortservice.army.mil.ng, selecting the SSCC option. The application is free of charge.

The Army has warned the public to disregard any recruitment announcement or application portal that appeared online before its official publication, urging applicants to rely only on information released through verified Nigerian Army channels.

nigerian-entertainment-four-deaths-week..title: Nigerian Entertainment Industry Mourns Four Deaths in One Week
nigerian-entertainment-four-deaths-week..excerpt: Nigeria's entertainment industry is mourning the deaths of four prominent figures — Saint Janet, Tope Osoba, Dimbo Atiya, and Coach Lara — who died within days of each other.
paras: Nigeria's entertainment industry is reeling from a devastating run of losses, with four well-known figures dying within days of one another in early August.

The wave of grief began with the death of juju musician Iyun Ajilore, popularly known as Saint Janet, following a brief illness. Celebrated for blending traditional juju and highlife rhythms with street humour and bold lyrics, she built a loyal following through her energetic stage presence. She is set to be laid to rest on August 13 at Saint James Anglican Church in Iperu Remo, Ogun State.

The industry had barely processed that loss when respected filmmaker Dimbo Atiya died at 53. Atiya was a well-regarded figure in Nigerian television, known for productions including Sons of the Caliphate, Halita, and The Rishantes that drew wide critical acclaim.

Actress Tope Osoba and Coach Lara also died within the same period, prompting an outpouring of tributes across the industry, including a candlelight vigil and Artists' Night held in Lagos to honour those who had passed.

nnpc-production-sharing-contract-framewo.title: NNPC to Roll Out New Contract Framework, Unlocking Up to $50bn in Offshore Oil Investment
nnpc-production-sharing-contract-framewo.excerpt: NNPC is set to implement a new Production Sharing Contract framework aimed at unlocking up to $50 billion in deep offshore oil and gas investment.
paras: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) is set to implement a new Production Sharing Contract (PSC) framework aimed at unlocking as much as $50 billion in deep offshore oil and gas investment, in one of the most significant policy shifts for Nigeria's upstream sector in recent years.

The move is expected to restructure how international and indigenous oil companies negotiate and operate offshore production agreements with the federal government, with officials framing it as a way to make Nigeria's deep offshore assets more commercially competitive against other oil-producing nations courting the same pool of global investment.

The announcement comes alongside separate news that President Bola Tinubu has signed a tax remission presidential order specifically targeting Nigeria's deep offshore oil projects, suggesting a coordinated push to make the sector more attractive at a moment when global capital for fossil fuel exploration has grown more selective.

Industry watchers say the real test will be implementation: previous reform efforts in Nigeria's oil sector have often been slowed by regulatory uncertainty and disputes between operators and the government over contract terms. NNPC has not yet released a detailed timeline for when the new framework will take effect.

npfl-euromatch-7-5m-sponsorship-deal.htm.title: NPFL Unveils EuroMatch as Title Sponsor in $7.5m Deal Ahead of New Season
npfl-euromatch-7-5m-sponsorship-deal.htm.excerpt: The Nigeria Premier Football League has unveiled EuroMatch as its official title sponsor in a three-year, $7.5 million naming-rights deal, with the new season kicking off August 28.
paras: The Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) has unveiled EuroMatch, a Poland-based gaming and technology investment company, as its official title sponsor in a naming-rights deal worth $7.5 million over three years.

The partnership was unveiled at a ceremony in Abuja attended by five former Super Eagles players, including members of Nigeria’s all-conquering 1994 Africa Cup of Nations-winning squad, alongside NFF President Alhaji Ibrahim Gusau. EuroMatch’s representative told the audience the company believed in Nigeria and the opportunities it offers, and expressed confidence in the league’s growth prospects.

The 2026/27 NPFL season kicks off on Friday, August 28, with a flag-off match between hosts Shooting Stars and visiting Inter Lagos in Ibadan. The remaining nine fixtures of the opening round will be played on Sunday, August 30.

nuee-shuts-eko-electricity-offices-lagos.title: NUEE Shuts Down Eko Electricity Offices in Lagos Over Unpaid Entitlements
nuee-shuts-eko-electricity-offices-lagos.excerpt: The National Union of Electricity Employees has shut down Eko Electricity Distribution Company offices in Lagos over poor conditions and unpaid entitlements.
paras: Members of the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) have shut down offices of the Eko Electricity Distribution Company (EKEDC) in Lagos in protest over what they described as poor working conditions and unpaid entitlements.
The industrial action disrupted operations at affected offices as workers pressed management to address their grievances.

ogogo-fidau-august-31-nollywood-tributes.title: Ogogo’s Family Announces August 31 Fidau as Nollywood Colleagues Pay Tribute
ogogo-fidau-august-31-nollywood-tributes.excerpt: The family of late actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, has announced a Fidau prayer for August 31, as Nollywood colleagues including Yinka Quadri and Dele Odule pay emotional tribute to the veteran actor.
paras: The family of veteran Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, has announced that a Fidau prayer in his honour will hold on August 31, 2026, as part of Islamic rites following his death on August 23 after a battle with stage-four cancer.

Veteran actor Yinka Quadri has recounted the emotional final moments he shared with his longtime friend and colleague before his passing, while fellow Nollywood veteran Dele Odule paid an emotional tribute, reflecting the close bonds within the Yoruba film industry that Ogogo helped build over more than four decades.

Nollywood is expected to hold a broader 40-day tribute in the actor’s honour in the weeks following his death, as colleagues and fans continue to mourn one of the industry’s most recognisable figures.

ogogo-taiwo-hassan-dies-66-cancer.html.title: Veteran Nollywood Actor Taiwo Hassan ‘Ogogo’ Dies at 66 After Cancer Battle
ogogo-taiwo-hassan-dies-66-cancer.html.excerpt: Veteran Yoruba Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, has died at the age of 66 after a battle with stage-four cancer, his family has confirmed.
paras: Veteran Nollywood actor, filmmaker and screenwriter Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, has died at the age of 66 after a battle with stage-four cancer. He died on Sunday, August 23, 2026.

His death was confirmed by his daughter, Kira Hassan, during an emotional Instagram Live session, and separately by veteran actor Jide Kosoko and a family friend. The news came just days after the actor’s family had publicly appealed for medical assistance as his condition deteriorated — and five days after the family had dismissed an earlier, false report of his death.

Born on October 31, 1959, in Ilaro, Ogun State, Ogogo built a career spanning more than four decades and became one of the most recognisable faces in Yoruba cinema.
